title: Latent Representation Learning from 3D Brain MRI for Latent Analysis and Prediction in Multiple Sclerosis.
abstract: Background Neurological diseases can lead to significant cognitive impairment. Linking magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-derived measures of brain structure with clinical assessments of cognitive function remains challenging, as conventional statistical methods and traditional machine learning approaches may struggle to capture complex relationships between brain structure and cognitive outcomes, hindering the development of reliable imaging biomarkers. Although deep learning methods offer greater predictive capabilities, their black-box nature limits interpretability, posing a major obstacle to clinical translation. New method Latent representation learning via generative models can provide informative representations and support deeper analysis and cognitive biomarker prediction. While standard generative adversarial networks and diffusion models primarily focus on generating images from random noise, variational autoencoders offer compact, probabilistic latent representations that are well suited for downstream tasks. In this study, we propose InfoVAE-Med3D, an adaptation of the InfoVAE framework for three-dimensional brain ​MRI to learn informative latent representations. By explicitly relaxing the mutual information regularization penalty between inputs and latent representations, our method aims to capture richer information from input MRI data, facilitating the analysis of brain-related characteristics and downstream prediction. Results We evaluate InfoVAE-Med3D on two datasets: a healthy control dataset ([Formula: see text]) containing chronological age and sex information, and a Multiple Sclerosis (MS) dataset ([Formula: see text]) collected from the Multiple Sclerosis Center of the First Medical Faculty, Charles University, Prague, containing chronological age, sex, and Symbol Digit Modalities Test (SDMT) scores. The learned latent representations capture information related to sex and brain volumetric features, including grey and white matter volumes, as reflected in sex-related clustering and smooth transitions in brain volume measures in two-dimensional visualizations. Through comprehensive evaluations, we demonstrate that InfoVAE-Med3D learns more informative latent representations, especially when the mutual information regularization penalty is completely removed. In this setting, the model generally outperforms other variational autoencoder variants in both MRI reconstruction and prediction of brain age and SDMT scores using support vector regression, while remaining competitive with deep learning-based predictive models, particularly on the MS dataset. Conclusion InfoVAE-Med3D provides informative latent representations from brain MRI data of both healthy controls and patients with MS. By improving predictive performance and providing interpretable insights into the learned latent representations, the proposed framework offers a promising approach for advancing biomarker discovery and the analysis of cognitive impairment in neurological diseases, particularly ​MS.

title: From Radical Resection to Organ Preservation in Locally Advanced Rectal Cancer: A Narrative Review of Risk-Adapted Management.
abstract: Purpose To synthesise evidence informing risk-adapted treatment and organ preservation in locally advanced rectal cancer. Methods This narrative review used targeted English-language searches of PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library through 31 March 2026, supplemented by targeted source verification in September 2026. Results Magnetic resonance imaging, mismatch repair status, recurrence risk, and patient preferences inform treatment selection. Total neoadjuvant therapy is established for higher-risk mismatch repair-proficient/microsatellite-stable disease. Chemoradiation followed by consolidation chemotherapy can improve organ-preservation probability compared with induction sequencing, without a demonstrated disease-free survival advantage. Selected lower-risk surgical candidates may receive chemotherapy with selective chemoradiation. Both short-course radiotherapy and long-course chemoradiation remain evidence-based options; the long-term locoregional failure signal in RAPIDO cannot be attributed to fractionation alone. Watch-and-wait requires multimodal confirmation of clinical complete response, intensive surveillance, and access to salvage surgery; oncological equivalence to immediate resection is unproven. Prospective dostarlimab data support non-operative management in selected mismatch repair-deficient rectal cancers, while long-term durability requires further evaluation. Conclusion Management should integrate tumour anatomy, biology, treatment response, and patient priorities. Organ preservation requires careful selection and structured follow-up, with treatment intensity individualised rather than applied uniformly.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Gallbladder Carcinoma: A Review of Research Studies and Clinical Evidence.
abstract: Background Gallbladder carcinoma (GBC) is the most common biliary tract malignancy and is usually diagnosed at an advanced stage. Artificial intelligence (AI), including radiomics, machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL), is increasingly applied to its diagnosis, surgical management and prognostication, but how far the reported performance can be trusted is unclear. Methods PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science, the Cochrane Library and Google Scholar were searched to 5 May 2026 using database-specific search strategies. Each primary prediction-model study was characterized separately by design, number of centers and validation type (internal, temporal or external). Results Of 31 primary AI studies in GBC, 29 were retrospective, 22 were single-center and 24 reported internal validation only. In independent test or external cohorts, DL and ML models discriminated benign from malignant gallbladder lesions with areas under the curve (AUCs) of approximately 0.80-0.89; a multicenter model distinguishing xanthogranulomatous cholecystitis from GBC achieved an external AUC of 0.88, and automated computed tomography (CT) segmentation an external Dice score of 0.76. The best recurrence model achieved an AUC of 0.76 on internal (random-split) validation; none of the reviewed prognostic models reported a quantified external-validation estimate. Intraoperative AI is technically feasible but has no outcome data, and federated learning has been tested only in simulation. Conclusion AI could plausibly assist several steps of GBC care, but the evidence is dominated by retrospective, single-center, internally validated studies from Asia, and metrics from different studies are not directly comparable. Prospective multicenter external validation, shared annotated datasets and standardized reporting are required before clinical adoption.

title: Postoperative ctDNA in Resectable Esophageal Squamous Cell Carcinoma: From Molecular Residual Disease Detection Toward Risk-Adapted Adjuvant Therapy and Surveillance.
abstract: Background Postoperative circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) is emerging as a marker of molecular residual disease (MRD) after curative-intent treatment for esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC). This review evaluates its ability to refine recurrence-risk assessment beyond pathological response and its potential role in guiding adjuvant therapy and surveillance. Methods A structured narrative review of studies evaluating perioperative and postoperative ctDNA in resectable ESCC was conducted using PubMed/MEDLINE through August 17, 2026, supplemented by citation tracking and clinical trial registry searches. Evidence was synthesized across treatment pathways, assay platforms, and postoperative management settings. Results Across ESCC cohorts using digital PCR, fixed next-generation sequencing panels, and personalized tumor-informed assays, postoperative ctDNA positivity consistently identifies patients at increased risk of recurrence, although estimates remain imprecise in small cohorts. Serial testing can detect molecular relapse months before radiographic recurrence. Integrated pathology-MRD models demonstrate additional risk stratification within both pathological complete response and non-completeresponse groups. Observational findings suggest, but do not establish, that MRD-positive patients may derive greater benefit from adjuvant immunotherapy. Conversely, MRD negativity alone does not justify omission of indicated adjuvant treatment. Conclusions Postoperative ctDNA provides complementary molecular risk information beyond conventional pathology in resectable ESCC. However, prospective MRD-guided trials are required before postoperative treatment or surveillance strategies can be routinely modified on the basis of ctDNA results alone.

title: Prognostic Value of Pre- and Post-Treatment PET-CT Metrics After Definitive Chemoradiation for Anal Canal Cancer.
abstract: Although post-treatment FDG-PET/CT is frequently obtained following definitive chemoradiation (CRT) for locally advanced anal canal cancer (LAACC), its prognostic utility remains uncertain. We hypothesized that quantitative PET/CT metrics would be associated with overall survival (OS) and that pre-treatment metabolic parameters would provide greater prognostic information than post-treatment metabolic response. We conducted a retrospective cohort study of patients with LAACC who underwent definitive CRT and both pre-treatment and post-treatment fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG) PET/CT. Quantitative PET metrics were extracted, including mean SUL, total lesion glycolysis (TLG), metabolic tumor volume (MTV), maximum SUL, and peak SUL. OS was estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method. Associations between PET-derived variables and OS were evaluated using univariable Cox proportional hazards regression, with optimal cutoffs identified using maximally selected rank statistics (MaxStat). Forty-five patients were included (median age 57.7 years), with post-treatment PET/CT performed at a median of 4.4 months following CRT. Lean body mass (HR 3.10, 95% CI 1.01-9.50; p = 0.049) and pre-treatment primary tumor mean SUL (HR 4.93, 95% CI 1.40-17.37; p = 0.013), size (HR 4.01, 95% CI 1.22-13.17; p = 0.022), TLG (HR 3.68, 95% CI 1.11-12.14; p = 0.033), and peak SUL (HR 3.31, 95% CI 1.02-10.72; p = 0.046) were associated with OS in exploratory univariable analyses. Post-treatment, higher weight (HR 4.94, 95% CI 1.06-22.96; p=0.041; cutoff 60.42 kg; N=45) and lean body mass (HR 4.82, 95% CI 1.06-21.90; p=0.042; cutoff 44.50 kg; N=44) were associated with worse OS. No post-treatment PET-derived metabolic parameters met the nominal threshold for statistical significance. Among patients with higher baseline metabolic activity, greater reduction in mean SUL following CRT demonstrated a nonsignificant trend toward improved OS. Pre-treatment FDG-PET/CT metabolic parameters demonstrated stronger associations with OS than post-treatment metabolic parameters in this exploratory cohort. Baseline tumor metabolic activity may provide useful prognostic information in patients with LAACC, warranting validation in larger prospective studies.

title: Deciphering intratumoral heterogeneity: An interpretable radiopathologic framework for lymph node staging in early-stage cervical cancer.
abstract: Preoperative assessment of lymph node metastasis (LNM) informs treatment planning in early-stage cervical cancer (CC). Traditional radiomics (TR) may obscure intratumoral heterogeneity. We developed multiparametric MRI habitat radiomics (HR) for LNM prediction and explored its histopathologic context. Patients underwent radical surgery and lymphadenectomy. Part I comprised 148 training and 63 test patients; Part II comprised 14 for spatially matched histopathology. Intratumoral voxels were clustered into habitats by K-means using T2-weighted imaging (T2WI), diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI), and contrast-enhanced T1-weighted imaging (CE-T1WI) signals. The number of habitats was selected using validation AUC. HR/TR scores and clinical-radiological predictors were integrated by logistic regression. AUC and accuracy were compared by DeLong's and χ² tests. Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) assessed contributions. Subregion-matched histopathology quantified Ki-67, CD3, CD31, and tumor-stroma ratio (TSR). LNM prevalence was 27.1% (61/225). The four-habitat HR model achieved a test AUC of 0.841 with 14 DWI/CE-T1WI-derived features. Test AUCs for clinical model (CL), TR, and HR + CL were 0.804, 0.784, and 0.890. HR + TR+CL achieved the highest AUC (0.902) and accuracy (87.30%), without a significant AUC difference from HR + CL (P = 0.277). SHAP ranked HR score above clinical lymph-node status, tumor diameter, and TR score. HR-3 exhibited highest Ki67 and lowest TSR, CD3, and CD31; HR-1 had highest TSR and lowest Ki67; HR-2 showed higher CD31 than HR-4. MRI-based HR may support preoperative LNM assessment in early-stage CC, with HR + CL representing a parsimonious candidate model for further evaluation. Spatially matched exploratory histopathology suggests possible regional tissue differences across MRI-defined habitats.

title: Proteomic and Metabolomic Profiling in Moyamoya Disease: A Systematic Review.
abstract: Moyamoya disease (MMD) is a progressive cerebrovascular disorder characterized by stenosis and occlusion of the internal carotid artery branches, leading to chronic ischemia and aberrant collateral vessel formation. Despite its clinical significance, the pathophysiology is not fully understood, and identification of MMD-related biomarkers may supplement invasive digital subtraction angiography, the current gold standard for diagnosis, as well as provide additional insights into prognosis and disease progression. High-throughput metabolomics and proteomics offer potential to elucidate disease mechanisms and identify diagnostic markers. Our goal is to systematically review the current literature on metabolomics and proteomics in MMD using high-throughput methods, identify candidate biomarkers, characterize implicated pathways, and assess the diagnostic and prognostic value of molecular signatures. We searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and Scopus databases through April 13, 2026, for studies analyzing serum or CSF from MMD patients using mass spectrometry, nuclear magnetic resonance, or immunoassays. Studies were included if they employed case-control, cohort, cross-sectional, or RCT designs in human subjects. Two reviewers independently screened titles, abstracts, and full texts, with disputes resolved by a third reviewer. Quality was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. We extracted the top differentially expressed proteins or metabolites, results of any enrichment pathway analyses, and demographics information from each study. From 3071 studies identified, 31 were included after removing 1558 duplicates and excluding 1482 irrelevant studies. Recurrent differentially expressed proteins implicated inflammatory signaling (CRABP-I, PDGF-BB, IL-7, complement proteins), angiogenesis (VEGF, Ang-2, MMP-9), and cytoskeletal remodeling (FLNA, ZYX, keratins), while consistent metabolomic signatures highlighted BCAA elevation, urea cycle disruption, and lipid remodeling. Pathway analyses recurrently implicated immune activation, endothelial dysfunction, cytoskeletal reorganization, hypoxia signaling, and metabolic reprogramming. Demographically, cohorts were predominantly adult, East Asian, and bilateral MMD, with a sample-size-weighted mean age of 40.0 years. High-throughput proteomics and metabolomics identified recurring molecular alterations in Moyamoya disease, commonly identifying inflammatory signaling, pathological angiogenesis, and cytoskeletal remodeling as potential pathophysiological mechanisms. Despite predominantly good-quality studies (mean Newcastle-Ottawa Scale 6.77 ± 0.67), major limitations included small sample sizes, single-center designs, and regional specificity. Validation in larger, ethnically diverse, multicenter cohorts is essential before clinical translation of candidate biomarkers and therapeutic targets.

title: Illuminating the future: energy-based focal therapies for prostate cancer.
abstract: Energy-based focal therapy is an image-guided, organ-preserving strategy intended to ablate clinically significant prostate cancer while limiting treatment-related injury to surrounding structures. This review critically examines high-intensity focused ultrasound (HIFU), cryoablation, irreversible electroporation (IRE), vascular-targeted photodynamic therapy (VTP), focal laser ablation (FLA), histotripsy, and electrochemotherapy (ECT), with emphasis on mechanisms, treatment planning, patient selection, oncological control, functional outcomes, and translational readiness. Multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging (mpMRI), combined with targeted and systematic biopsy, is central to defining disease extent and assessing treatment response. Although prospective cohorts report encouraging medium-term outcomes for several established modalities, variation in eligibility criteria, ablation margins, surveillance protocols, biopsy requirements, and failure definitions limits cross-modality comparisons. Randomized evidence for padeliporfin-based photodynamic therapy demonstrates disease modification relative to active surveillance in selected men with low-risk disease, but does not establish equivalence to radical prostatectomy or radiotherapy. Residual and out-of-field cancer, repeat treatment, and the scarcity of long-term comparative data remain limitations. Radiomics, artificial intelligence, and molecular biomarkers, including DNA-repair and androgen-receptor alterations, may improve risk stratification and treatment personalization; however, their clinical utility requires external validation, reproducible workflows, and governance. Integration with systemic therapy, radiotherapy, or immunotherapy remains investigational, and evidence from advanced disease should not be extrapolated directly to localized cancer. Histotripsy and ECT require further prostate-specific clinical validation. Responsible implementation depends on multidisciplinary selection, transparent counseling, standardized oncological and patient-reported endpoints, prospective trials or registries, and predefined surveillance and salvage pathways. Focal therapy should therefore be regarded as a selective, evidence-developing treatment strategy rather than an established substitute for definitive whole-gland treatment.

title: Prognostic value of integrated dynamic NLR and [ 18 F]FDG-PET/CT parameters in resectable non-small cell lung cancer treated with neoadjuvant immunotherapy plus chemotherapy.
abstract: Objective This study aimed to evaluate the prognostic value of dynamic [ 18 F]FDG PET/CT metabolic parameters and the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), individually and in combination, in patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) receiving neoadjuvant immunotherapy plus chemotherapy. Methods We retrospectively analyzed 168 NSCLC patients treated with neoadjuvant immunochemotherapy followed by surgery. Pre- and post-treatment PET metabolic parameters assessed by iPERCIST and peripheral blood NLR were collected. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis and Kaplan-Meier survival analysis with Cox regression were performed to identify predictors of disease-free survival (DFS). Results During a median follow-up of 25.2 months (95% CI, 21.0-29.3 months), 59 patients experienced recurrence. Post-treatment PET metabolic parameters, their changes, and post-treatment NLR were significantly associated with DFS. Among these parameters, ΔSUVmax and post-treatment NLR were identified as independent prognostic factors. Patients were stratified into three risk groups according to the combination of ΔSUVmax and post-treatment NLR, with significantly different DFS outcomes among groups (p = 0.001). Patients achieving iCMR/iPMR according to iPERCIST criteria showed longer DFS than those without favorable metabolic response (p = 0.005) . Conclusions Dynamic PET metabolic parameters, and post-treatment NLR hold significant prognostic value following neoadjuvant immunotherapy plus chemotherapy in NSCLC. A combined model integrating PET metabolic parameters and post-treatment NLR stratified patients into distinct risk groups, suggesting potential utility in postoperative risk assessment.

title: Monte Carlo-based three-dimensional dose evaluation for rotational cerebral angiography: peak dose to brain and skin and Dose-Volume Histogram (DVH) analysis of the brain.
abstract: Background and purpose Rotational cerebral angiography produces complex, nonuniform dose distributions; the mean brain dose may not sufficiently represent localized high-dose regions. This study aimed to visualize three-dimensional dose distributions in the brain and skin using PHITS, estimate peak brain dose (PBD) and peak skin dose (PSD), and evaluate the brain dose distribution using dose-volume histogram (DVH) analysis. Materials and methods X-ray spectra for 3D digital subtraction angiography (3D-DSA, 70 kV) and cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT, 109 kV) were generated using SpekPy and implemented in PHITS. A rotational irradiation model covering approximately 200° was constructed using a multisource approach based on projection-dependent tube current-time product values. The model was validated using a PMMA phantom. Three-dimensional dose distributions were calculated using the adult male mesh-type reference computational phantom; PBD, PSD, and brain DVH indices were evaluated. Results Calculated doses agreed with measured values within 5.2%. Dose concentrations were mainly observed in the occipital region. The PBD and PSD were 25.1 and 44.1 mGy for 3D-DSA and 101.3 and 139.1 mGy for CBCT, respectively. The PBD was 3.3 times higher than the mean brain dose for 3D-DSA and 2.3 times higher for CBCT. DVH analysis showed that CBCT shifted the brain-dose distribution toward higher-dose regions, with D10% values of 14.9 and 70.0 mGy for 3D-DSA and CBCT, respectively. Conclusions PHITS-based three-dimensional dose evaluation allowed localized high-dose regions in the brain and skin to be visualized and quantified. DVH analysis complemented the peak dose assessment by providing volumetric information on the brain-dose distribution.

title: Quantitative assessment of diaphragmatic motion in COPD using pixel-wise optical flow analysis of cine MRI.
abstract: Diaphragmatic dysfunction is a key determinant of dyspnea and impaired respiratory mechanics in patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD); however, objective quantification remains limited. This study quantitatively assessed diaphragmatic motion in COPD using pixel-wise optical flow analysis of sagittal cine magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Sagittal cine MRI of the right hemidiaphragm during quiet breathing was performed in 35 patients with COPD and 9 healthy participants. Optical flow was computed within the diaphragmatic region of interest after semiautomatic segmentation. Three indices were derived during expiration: the direction agreement ratio (DAR; proportion of pixels showing upward motion), the proportion of motionless areas (PMA), and mean diaphragmatic velocity (MDV). These indices were compared between patients with COPD and healthy participants across Global Initiative for Chronic Obstructive Lung Disease (GOLD) stages and were stratified by the presence of visually assessed paradoxical motion. Pulmonary function associations were evaluated. Compared with healthy participants, patients with COPD showed a lower DAR, higher PMA, and reduced MDV (all p < 0.001). The DAR decreased and the PMA increased with advancing GOLD stages. Patients with paradoxical motion exhibited a lower DAR and higher PMA than those without paradoxical motion. DAR and PMA were correlated with FEV 1 %pred (ρ = 0.71 and - 0.71, respectively), whereas MDV correlated negatively with RV %pred (ρ = - 0.79). Pixel-wise optical flow analysis using cine MRI provides a potential quantitative framework for evaluating diaphragmatic dysfunction in COPD by capturing synchrony, regional immobility, and motion velocity.

title: Metabolomic Analysis of Patients with Coronary Artery Disease and Acute Myocardial Infarction by Using Nuclear Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy.
abstract: This cross-sectional exploratory study investigates the potential of metabolomics to differentiate between stable coronary artery disease (CAD) and acute myocardial infarction (AMI) through Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (NMR) spectroscopic analysis. The study identifies distinct metabolic profiles for each condition, revealing significant variations in metabolite levels, particularly lactic acid, which is a key metabolic product of anaerobic glycolysis, emerges as a prominent marker in AMI patients, reflecting acute ischemic stress and providing insight into adverse outcomes associated with high lactate levels. Another metabolite found in the present study was hypoxanthine, which is key biomarker for myocardial ischemia. These findings underscore the potential of metabolomics in combination with pathway analysis in distinguishing between CAD and AMI and highlight the metabolic dysregulation that occurs in these diseases. Our results suggest that these metabolites could serve as potential biomarkers, paving the way for personalized prognostic and diagnostic strategies. Further large-scale studies are necessary to validate these findings and incorporate them into clinical practice.

title: Predicting neoadjuvant chemotherapy efficacy in triple-negative breast cancer using DCE-MRI and mammographic texture.
abstract: Objective This study aimed to develop and validate a predictive model integrating dynamic contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (DCE-MRI) kinetic features and digital breast tomosynthesis (DBT) texture features for predicting pathological complete response (pCR) following neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC) in patients with triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC). Additionally, its predictive performance was compared with that of single-modality models. Materials and methods A total of 360 patients with pathologically confirmed TNBC who received NAC between January 2022 and December 2025 were retrospectively and consecutively collected. Patients were randomly allocated to a training set (n = 252) and a validation set (n = 108) at a 7:3 ratio. Pre-NAC DCE-MRI kinetic and DBT texture features were extracted. After feature selection using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression, DCE-MRI and DBT radiomics scores (Rad-scores) were constructed. A nomogram prediction model was then developed using multivariable logistic regression incorporating clinicopathological and laboratory indicators. Model discrimination, calibration, and clinical net benefit were evaluated using the receiver operating characteristic curves, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis, respectively. These results were subsequently compared with those of a clinical-only model and single-modality combined models. Results The pCR rates in the training and validation sets were 41.67% and 40.74%, respectively. Multivariable logistic regression identified Ki-67 proliferation index, maximum tumor diameter, background parenchymal enhancement score, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, lactate dehydrogenase level, DCE-Rad score, and DBT-Rad score as independent predictors of pCR (P < 0.05). The dual-modality nomogram achieved area under the curve (AUC) values of 0.784 (95% CI: 0.718-0.851) in the training set and 0.759 (95% CI: 0.644-0.873) in the validation set, outperforming the clinical-only model (0.727), the clinical plus DCE-Rad score model (0.761), and the clinical plus DBT-Rad score model (0.766). Calibration curves showed good agreement between predicted probabilities and actual outcomes. Furthermore, decision curve analysis confirmed the clinical net benefit of the proposed model. Conclusions The multimodal radiomics fusion model based on DCE-MRI kinetic and DBT texture features effectively predicts pCR following NAC in TNBC patients. Its predictive performance is superior to that of single-modality models. Consequently, this model offers a non-invasive imaging tool for individualized pretreatment efficacy assessment. Nevertheless, further multicenter external validation is required to confirm its generalizability. For now, it should be viewed as a decision‑support aid that informs rather than dictates treatment choices, with specific actionable thresholds to be refined in future prospective studies.

title: Nonlinear association between age and volumetric breast density in Japanese women.
abstract: Background Volumetric breast density (VBD) is influenced by age, body mass index (BMI), and reproductive factors, yet the shape of the age-VBD association and age-specific VBD distributions in Japanese women remain incompletely characterized. We examined the associations of age, BMI, menopausal status, and parity with software-derived VBD and characterized age-specific VBD distributions, including the proportion of women with VBD ≥ 7.5%. Methods This cross-sectional study included 719 asymptomatic Japanese women undergoing screening mammography (mean age, 58.7 ± 12.6 years; range, 20-87 years) in whom no breast lesion was identified. VBD was quantified using Volpara Density. Age was modeled using restricted cubic splines, adjusted for BMI, menopausal status, and parity. Regression analyses used 672 complete cases. Mean VBD ≥ 7.5% defined volumetrically dense breasts. Results Overall, 72.7% (523/719) had VBD ≥ 7.5%. Mean VBD was 17.34%, 13.41%, 11.01%, and 11.72% at ages 40-49, 50-59, 60-69, and 70-79 years, respectively, and 16.81% versus 11.85% in pre- versus postmenopausal women. Age was associated with VBD (P < 0.001), with significant nonlinearity (P = 0.027); adjusted VBD was lower with increasing age until the mid-60s and then largely plateaued. Higher BMI (β = -1.08; 95% CI, - 1.20 to - 0.97; P < 0.001) and parity (β = -2.21; 95% CI, - 3.43 to - 0.98; P < 0.001) were independently associated with lower VBD, whereas menopausal status was not (β = -1.07; 95% CI, - 2.85 to 0.71; P = 0.239). Conclusions Age was nonlinearly associated with VBD in Japanese women, plateauing after the mid-60s. VBD ≥ 7.5% was common, while BMI and parity remained independently associated with lower VBD.

title: Towards Reliable Measurement of Cerebellar Morphology: A Comparative Assessment of Segmentation Pipelines.
abstract: Characterizing cerebellar morphology is fundamental for accurately mapping its structure and function across individuals, yet remains challenging due to its densely foliated architecture. Although multiple automated segmentation pipelines exist, the measurement reproducibility of these tools has not been comprehensively benchmarked. We conducted a systematic assessment of reliability for cerebellar morphology estimates using four commonly used pipelines: one classic parcellation method (CERES), two deep-learning methods (ACAPULCO, DeepCERES), and one voxel-based morphometry toolbox (SUIT). Leveraging the HNU dataset, which provides MRI scans for ten timepoints per individual over a month, we evaluated the test-retest reliability for each of the four pipelines using ReX, an integrative tool for quantifying and optimizing measurement reliability and individual differences. We quantified intra- and inter-individual variability, as well as the Intraclass Correlation Coefficient (ICC), for each pipeline at both global and region-of-interest levels. We used two pools of data: a common dataset of 12 subjects x 5 sessions to benchmark all the pipelines, and method-specific datasets including pools of subjects with 5 valid sessions for each pipeline to assess the generalizability of our findings. Overall, all pipelines yielded highly reliable segmentation volumes (ICC > 0.87). DeepCERES demonstrated the most consistent performance across all metrics and subject pools, while SUIT achieved the highest ICC on the common dataset but showed decreased reliability when evaluated on a larger subject pool. Importantly, our analysis highlighted substantial heterogeneity in reliability across lobules for each method. Lobule X consistently showed reduced reliability whereas lobules I-V, VI, Crus I, IX, and VIIIB were reliably estimated across all pipelines. While all pipelines demonstrated strong reliability, DeepCERES showed the most robust and consistent performance overall. Substantial lobule-specific variability and method-dependent failure rates underscore the need for reliability-aware pipeline selection to optimize cerebellar morphology estimation in research.

title: Type Vb double common bile duct complicated by gallbladder cancer.
abstract: Double common bile duct (DCBD) is an extremely rare biliary anomaly with subtype-dependent oncological risk. We report a case of DCBD (Choi classification type Vb) complicated by gallbladder cancer. A 75-year-old woman was incidentally found to have a gallbladder fundus tumor on screening ultrasonography. Preoperative imaging suggested gallbladder cancer within clinical T3 or less. Biliary evaluation by magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography (MRCP), drip infusion cholangiography-computed tomography (DIC-CT), and endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) confirmed Choi type Vb DCBD without pancreaticobiliary maljunction (PBM). The patient underwent open extended cholecystectomy with a stepwise intraoperative strategy guided by frozen section analysis. Frozen section confirmed adenocarcinoma; as the cystic duct margin was tumor-free, lymph node dissection was limited to the cystic duct nodes without hepatoduodenal ligament dissection. Final pathology: adenocarcinoma (well to moderately differentiated), pT1b, pN0 (0/3), pStage IB (Union for International Cancer Control [UICC] 9th edition), pR0. The patient was discharged on postoperative day 11 and remained recurrence-free at 6 months. To our knowledge, this is the fourth reported type Vb DCBD case in the English-language literature and the first associated with gallbladder cancer. Preoperative evaluation of biliary anatomy, including PBM status, and a stepwise intraoperative approach are essential for safe and oncologically appropriate management.

title: Multifocal primary hepatic small cell neuroendocrine carcinoma treated with sequential systemic therapies.
abstract: Primary hepatic small cell neuroendocrine carcinoma (PHNEC) is an exceptionally rare malignancy with no established systemic treatment. An 83-year-old man with elevated hepatobiliary enzyme levels was found to have multiple liver tumors. Liver biopsy revealed small cell neuroendocrine carcinoma with positive immunohistochemical staining for insulinoma-associated protein 1. Systemic imaging, including chest computed tomography and 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/computed tomography, and upper and lower gastrointestinal endoscopy revealed no definite extrahepatic primary site, supporting a clinical diagnosis of multifocal PHNEC. Serum CA19-9, SPan-1, DUPAN-2, and neuron-specific enolase (NSE) levels were elevated at diagnosis. Treatment with carboplatin, etoposide, and atezolizumab resulted in marked tumor regression and substantial decreases in these tumor markers. However, disease progression occurred during atezolizumab maintenance approximately four months after treatment initiation. Gemcitabine plus S-1 (tegafur/gimeracil/oteracil) was subsequently administered, followed by amrubicin after further progression. During second-line therapy, CA19-9 and SPan-1 levels transiently decreased, whereas NSE increased before radiological progression. The patient ultimately died of progressive disease approximately 11 months after diagnosis. Although the initial radiological response was not durable and the contribution of atezolizumab remains uncertain, this case highlights the clinical course of multifocal PHNEC treated with sequential systemic therapies and the potential utility of multiple tumor markers for monitoring disease activity.

title: Cardiac amyloidosis: the role of multimodality imaging.
abstract: Cardiac amyloidosis is an increasingly recognized cause of heart failure, driven by advances in diagnostic techniques and the emergence of disease-modifying therapies. Early and accurate diagnosis is essential as timely treatment influences prognosis. Although endomyocardial biopsy remains the reference standard, non-invasive imaging has become central to the diagnostic pathway and disease evaluation.This review summarizes the contemporary role of multimodality imaging in cardiac amyloidosis. Echocardiography remains the first-line imaging modality and can provide important diagnostic clues, including increased ventricular wall thickness and apical sparing on strain analyses. CMR enables detailed tissue characterization, allowing non-invasive assessment of myocardial amyloid burden and disease progression. Bone scintigraphy has revolutionized the diagnosis of transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy by enabling a reliable non-biopsy diagnosis after exclusion of light-chain amyloidosis. Emerging PET tracers may further improve early detection, quantification of amyloid burden, and monitoring of treatment response.The integration of multimodality imaging has fundamentally changed the diagnostic and therapeutic landscape of cardiac amyloidosis, facilitating earlier recognition, improved risk stratification, and longitudinal disease monitoring. As novel therapies continue to emerge, advanced imaging techniques are expected to play an increasingly important role in personalized management and evaluation of therapeutic response.

title: A prospective study of acoustic voice analysis and 24-h pH-metry for detecting gastroesophageal reflux disease in idiopathic hoarseness.
abstract: Background and aim Gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) is a known contributor to chronic hoarseness. This study aimed at determining the prevalence of GERD in patients with idiopathic hoarseness using endoscopy and 24-h impedance pH monitoring and to assessing associated acoustic voice parameters. Methods In this prospective study, 242 patients with hoarseness were screened, of which 40 (n = 40) with idiopathic hoarseness were selected for detailed evaluation. All underwent video laryngoscopy, acoustic voice analysis, esophagogastroduodenoscopy, esophageal manometry and 24-h impedance pH-metry. GERD diagnosis was based on findings such as LA grade B/C/D esophagitis, Barrett's esophagus, peptic strictures or abnormal acid exposure time and DeMeester scores. Acoustic parameters including jitter, shimmer and noise-to-harmonics ratio (NHR) were analyzed. Results Among 40 participants selected for evaluation, GERD was diagnosed in 25 (62.5%). Univariate binary logistic regression revealed significant associations between a confirmed GERD diagnosis and clinical severity markers, including the presence of erosive esophagitis (p = 0.02) and elevated reflux symptom index scores (p = 0.002). Crucially, objective acoustic voice analysis demonstrated robust correlations with reflux status. Patients with GERD exhibited distinct, quantifiable vocal fold instability, evidenced by significantly elevated absolute jitter (p = 0.03), jitter percentage (p = 0.04), shimmer percentage (p = 0.02) and noise-to-harmonics ratio (NHR) (p = 0.04) compared to non-GERD individuals. Conclusion GERD was identified in 62.5% of patients within this highly selected idiopathic hoarseness cohort. Both clinical indicators and objective acoustic perturbation measures-specifically jitter, shimmer and NHR-demonstrated significant, unadjusted univariate associations with GERD. These findings highlight that reflux causes measurable vocal disruption, suggesting acoustic voice analysis holds promising potential as a non-invasive adjunctive tool for evaluating laryngeal reflux. However, larger, controlled multi-center studies are necessary to perform multi-variable adjustment and firmly establish the clinical diagnostic role of these parameters.

title: Physical image quality of normal- and super-resolution deep learning reconstruction in lung CT: a task-based phantom study.
abstract: To quantitatively compare the physical image quality characteristics of normal-resolution deep learning reconstruction (NR-DLR) and super-resolution deep learning reconstruction (SR-DLR) in lung CT, with particular emphasis on task-based detectability. A 180-mm TOS-SS phantom was scanned at four dose levels (CTDIvol: 11.2, 5.6, 2.6 and 1.0 mGy). Images were reconstructed using NR-DLR (AiCE) and SR-DLR (PIQE) at three noise reduction levels (Levels 1-3), with 512- and 1024-matrix settings at display fields-of-view (D-FOVs) of 320 and 180 mm. Spatial resolution was assessed using the task transfer function (TTF), noise characteristics were evaluated using the noise power spectrum (NPS), and task performance was quantified using the non-prewhitening detectability index (d') for a 10-mm, 130-HU disk target. An additional analysis was performed using a 3 mm, 130 HU target to evaluate task dependence. AiCE demonstrated higher f₅₀ values and characteristic frequency enhancement (overshoot), whereas PIQE exhibited a monotonic TTF profile and lower high-frequency noise components. Despite lower f₅₀ values, PIQE yielded higher d' values in most reconstruction settings for the 10 mm task. For the 3 mm task, the difference in d' between PIQE and AiCE was reduced, and their relative relationship was reversed in some reconstruction settings. NR-DLR and SR-DLR demonstrated distinct resolution-noise characteristics in lung CT. Despite lower f₅₀ values, SR-DLR yielded higher task-based detectability in most reconstruction settings for the 10 mm task; however, the relative detectability performance of NR-DLR and SR-DLR was task dependent.

title: Long-Term Outcomes of Image-Guided Superficial Radiation Therapy for Stage I-II Nonmelanoma Skin Cancer: A Real-World Retrospective Cohort Study.
abstract: Introduction Image-guided superficial radiation therapy (IGSRT) is increasingly utilized for the treatment of nonmelanoma skin cancer (NMSC). Although prior studies, including extensive multi-institutional cohorts, have reported local control rates exceeding 99% for early-stage basal cell carcinoma (BCC) and squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) treated with IGSRT, data on long-term efficacy and adverse reactions remain limited. This study aims to evaluate the long-term efficacy and safety of IGSRT for stage I-II BCCs and SCCs. Methods This retrospective cohort study analyzed outcomes from stage I-II BCC and SCC tumors treated with IGSRT per the Ladd-Yu protocol between 2016 and 2023. The primary aim was to assess freedom from recurrence (FFR), via Kaplan-Meier (KM) survival analysis at 2 and 5 years. The secondary aim was to compare the Radiation Therapy Oncology Group (RTOG) toxicity scores of three IGSRT dosing protocols: 3 fractions/week, 4 fractions/week, and 5 fractions/week. Results A total of 10,248 patients with 13,357 lesions were included in this study (8729 BCCs and 4628 SCCs). The Kaplan-Meier estimated FFR was 99.7% and 99.6% for stage I and stage II lesions, respectively (n = 8485 NMSCs). Similarly, 5-year FFR for stage I and II lesions were both 99.7% (n = 2427 NMSCs). There were 3697 patients (36.1%) lost to follow-up at 2 years and 2942 (61.5%) lost to follow-up at 5 years. No statistically significant differences in FFR were observed between stages (P > 0.05) within histologic type (i.e., BCC or SCC). Most lesions (97.5%) developed mild RTOG toxicities (RTOG 0-2), while 2.5% developed severe toxicities (RTOG 3-4). NMSCs had statistically similar probability of severe toxicities, regardless of the number of radiation fractions/week (P > 0.05). Patients with tumors of the head or neck had reduced risk of severe toxicities (P = 0.004) while patients with stage II tumors were more likely to experience severe toxicities (P < 0.001). Conclusions These findings confirm the durable long-term control of NMSC treated with IGSRT following the Ladd-Yu protocol inclusive of high-resolution dermal ultrasound, with predominantly mild adverse reactions. These data support the use of IGSRT as a primary treatment of stage I and II NMSC lesions.

title: Diagnostic Accuracy of Shallow Irregular Retinal Pigment Epithelium Elevation Phenotypes for Detecting Macular Neovascularization in Central Serous Chorioretinopathy: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: Introduction Macular neovascularization (MNV) complicating central serous chorioretinopathy (CSC) may be subtle and difficult to distinguish from chronic pachychoroid-related retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) alterations using structural optical coherence tomography (OCT) alone. Shallow irregular RPE elevation phenotypes, including flat irregular RPE detachment and the double-layer sign (DLS), may serve as structural OCT markers of MNV. This systematic review and diagnostic test accuracy (DTA) meta-analysis evaluated the diagnostic performance of these phenotypes for detecting MNV in eyes with CSC. Methods Nine databases were searched through 19 May 2026, without language restriction. Eligible studies included eyes with CSC, evaluated a shallow irregular RPE elevation phenotype as the index test, used OCT angiography (OCTA) alone or within a multimodal imaging framework to establish MNV status, and provided extractable 2 × 2 diagnostic data. Anatomically overlapping but nonidentical OCT phenotypes were harmonized into a common shallow irregular RPE elevation category for quantitative synthesis. Summary sensitivity and specificity were estimated using a hierarchical DTA model. Risk of bias and applicability were assessed using QUADAS-2. The review was prospectively registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261404129). Results Nine studies comprising 671 eyes were included in the primary DTA analysis. Shallow irregular RPE elevation phenotypes were present in 130 of 138 eyes with MNV and absent in 352 of 533 eyes without MNV. For the harmonized phenotype, the model-based summary sensitivity was 98% (95% confidence interval [CI], 77-100%) and summary specificity was 69% (95% CI, 53-81%). Across scenario-based sensitivity analyses, summary sensitivity ranged from 97 to 99%, whereas specificity ranged from 61 to 66%. Estimates should be interpreted in the context of heterogeneous phenotype definitions and reference standards, enriched or selected study populations, and sparse false-negative observations. Conclusions The harmonized shallow irregular RPE elevation phenotype on structural OCT is associated with concurrent MNV in CSC but is not sufficiently specific to establish neovascularization. Suspicious morphology warrants clinical assessment and, when appropriate, confirmatory vascular imaging; absence of the phenotype cannot reliably exclude MNV. The apparently high sensitivity should be interpreted cautiously because of selection and spectrum bias, heterogeneous reference-standard implementation, and sparse false-negative observations. Prospero registration CRD420261404129.

title: Bilateral pheochromocytoma and multiple paragangliomas in a patient with a heterozygous SDHD mutation: A challenging case report.
abstract: Hereditary pheochromocytoma and paraganglioma (PPGL) are rare, genetically determined neuroendocrine tumors that often present at a young age. Their multifocal nature poses diagnostic and therapeutic challenges and warrants early genetic testing. A 26-year-old man was referred for cervical and mediastinal paragangliomas. Computed tomography scan revealed multiple cervical and mediastinal paragangliomas and bilateral pheochromocytoma. Plasma normetanephrine was 2616 ng/L (13 times the upper normal limit). Genetic testing confirmed an SDHD mutation. After alpha- and beta-blockade, the patient underwent bilateral adrenalectomy and mediastinal paraganglioma resection under cardiopulmonary bypass. Octreotide therapy was initiated due to inoperability of cervical paragangliomas.However, a loss of therapeutic response was observed one year after the initiation of somatostatin analogue. Radiotherapy was then considered for the cervical paragangliomas. This case underlines the complexity of PPGL management in patients with SDHD mutation. Multifocal disease demands individualized, multidisciplinary strategies and long-term follow-up to minimize morbidity and optimize outcomes in young patients.

title: A metaheuristic-based ensemble framework for osteoporosis classification using knee X-ray images.
abstract: Osteoporosis is a progressive skeletal disorder characterized by reduced bone strength and increased fracture susceptibility, while its early identification from conventional radiographic images remains challenging because clinically relevant structural and textural variations can be subtle. This study proposes OsteoEnsembleNet, an ensemble stacking machine learning framework for automated osteoporosis classification using knee radiographs. The framework employs an Adaptive Unscented Kalman Filter (AUKF) for adaptive image quality enhancement, followed by a Hybrid Improved Beluga Whale Optimizer-Modified Fuzzy C-Means (HiBWmFCM) method for knee region segmentation. Multiple complementary feature domains, including morphological, statistical, gray-level co-occurrence matrix (GLCM), texture, and local binary pattern (LBP) descriptors, are subsequently extracted and optimized using HRSWaO feature selection. To improve classification robustness, predictions from seven heterogeneous classifiers-artificial neural network (ANN), k-nearest neighbors (KNN), support vector machine (SVM), random forest (RF), gradient boosting, XGBoost, and AdaBoost-are integrated through a logistic regression-based stacking meta-classifier. Experiments were conducted on publicly available Knee X-ray Osteoporosis Database. On the 80:20 patient-level split, the proposed framework achieved 97.92% accuracy, 98.96% precision, 96.67% recall, 97.72% F1-score, 96.01% MCC, and 95.63% Jaccard index, with a Hamming loss of 2.08%. The results demonstrate that combining adaptive preprocessing, targeted segmentation, complementary radiographic feature representation, feature selection, and heterogeneous ensemble learning can provide consistent discrimination among Normal, Osteopenia, and Osteoporosis categories from knee X-ray images. The framework is intended as an automated image-based decision-support approach and does not directly replace quantitative bone density assessment.

title: A proposed ultrasound classification of distal pectoralis major injuries: a pictorial essay.
abstract: Distal pectoralis major (PM) injuries are increasingly recognised in sports medicine but remain difficult to characterise on imaging. We retrospectively reviewed 119 distal PM injuries diagnosed by ultrasound at a single centre between September 2022 and September 2026, all examined by the same operator. Based on the PM connective skeleton, namely the pectoralis major tendon (PMT), the deltopectoral tendon (DPT) and the intramuscular connective trident, we propose a descriptive sonographic classification distinguishing complete PMT tears with an intact DPT (31.1%), combined complete PMT and DPT tears (19.3%), partial-width PMT tears (16.8%) and intramuscular injuries with an intact PMT (32.8%), graded by lamina involvement. At surgery (79 injuries), ultrasound and operative categories agreed in 71, disagreed in 2, and operative findings were indeterminate in 6. This pictorial essay illustrates the sonographic landmarks, dynamic manoeuvres and appearance of each pattern. The classification has not yet been validated for reproducibility or treatment utility.

title: A scoping review of micro-ultrasound in male infertility: mapping the evidence from testicular microarchitecture to the distal seminal tract.
abstract: Micro-ultrasound (micro-US), a 29-MHz modality with a resolution of about 70 µm established in prostate cancer diagnosis, and related very-high-resolution ultrasound techniques could refine the evaluation of male infertility, but their use in this field has not been mapped. This scoping review, reported according to PRISMA-ScR, charted the evidence on micro-US, very-high-frequency (≥ 20 MHz) ultrasound and ultrasound localisation microscopy (ULM) for the diagnosis and prognosis of male infertility, from testicular microarchitecture to the distal seminal tract. On 1 October 2026, 38 web-based queries and citation tracking covered sources indexing PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science and Google Scholar. Of the 91 records screened, nine sources were included: four ULM studies, three reports of 36-46-MHz quantitative ultrasound (two preprints, one conference abstract), one high-frequency study with histological correlation and one registered 29-MHz micro-US trial without results. Human cohorts ranged from 7 to 94 men. ULM vessel diameter and density were lower in non-obstructive than in obstructive azoospermia (area under the curve, AUC, 0.81-0.95), and ULM detected the response to gonadotrophin therapy earlier than testicular volume in seven men. Quantitative features discriminated sperm presence (AUC 0.77-0.93). No study examined the vas deferens, epididymis, seminal vesicles, ejaculatory ducts or varicocele; none was externally validated, and none reported retrieval, pregnancy or live birth outcomes. The evidence is early, small and testis centred, and these methods remain investigational. Prospective validation against histology and surgical sperm retrieval, with clinical outcomes, and exploration of the distal seminal tract are priorities.

title: Ultrasound elastography of pediatric cervical lymph nodes: a systematic review of clinical potential and current limitations.
abstract: Aims Cervical lymphadenopathy is common in children and encompasses reactive, inflammatory, infectious, and malignant conditions. Ultrasound elastography assesses tissue mechanical properties and may complement conventional ultrasonography. This systematic review aimed to critically evaluate the evidence on cervical lymph node elastography in pediatric patients. Methods PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched on October 8, 2026. Reporting followed PRISMA 2020; the protocol was not prospectively registered. Risk of bias was assessed with QUADAS-2 in diagnostic accuracy studies, and findings were synthesized narratively. Results Five studies involving 484 pediatric participants were included. Three investigated benign-malignant differentiation and two evaluated inflammatory conditions, using strain elastography, acoustic radiation force impulse imaging, shear wave elastography, or point shear wave elastography. Studies addressing malignancy reported promising diagnostic performance, but numerical inconsistencies in two publications undermined confidence in their accuracy estimates. Four studies assessed with QUADAS-2 showed high or unclear risk of bias in at least one domain; the fifth, lacking diagnostic accuracy outcomes, was assessed descriptively. Increased stiffness occurred in both malignant and benign inflammatory or infectious lymphadenopathy, limiting its specificity for malignancy. Differences in clinical populations, techniques, diagnostic objectives, and reference standards precluded quantitative synthesis. Conclusions Ultrasound elastography may complement conventional assessment of pediatric cervical lymphadenopathy, but current evidence does not support universal stiffness thresholds or standalone diagnostic use. Prospective pediatric studies with standardized protocols and external validation are needed to establish its incremental value beyond conventional ultrasonography.

title: Durable Treatment-Free Remission in BRCA1-Associated Metastatic Triple-Negative Breast Cancer with Brain and Radiologically Diagnosed Hepatic Metastases: A Case Report.
abstract: Introduction Metastatic triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is associated with aggressive clinical behavior and poor survival, particularly in patients with brain and visceral metastases. We describe an exceptionally durable treatment-free remission in a young woman with metastatic TNBC and a subsequently identified pathogenic germline BRCA1 variant. Methods We retrospectively reviewed the patient's clinical course, radiological and histopathological findings, systemic and local treatments, genetic testing, and long-term follow-up. Results In 2008, the patient was diagnosed with grade 3 triple-negative invasive ductal carcinoma and hepatic lesions considered metastatic based on computed tomography (CT), magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), and multidisciplinary assessment. Following six cycles of fluorouracil, doxorubicin, and cyclophosphamide (FAC), the hepatic lesions regressed. In 2009, she developed a solitary, histologically confirmed left frontal brain metastasis, which was surgically resected and treated with postoperative radiotherapy. Subsequent breast and hepatic disease progression was treated with 15 cycles of docetaxel plus bevacizumab, resulting in a marked radiological response. Following isolated locoregional progression in 2011, without radiologically active distant disease, she underwent modified radical mastectomy with axillary dissection followed by locoregional radiotherapy. A pathogenic germline BRCA1 variant was identified in 2020. She has received no systemic anticancer therapy since December 2010 and remained in complete clinical and radiological remission as of June 2026, more than 17 years after diagnosis of the brain metastasis. Conclusions This case documents an exceptionally prolonged treatment-free remission in metastatic TNBC despite a history of radiologically diagnosed hepatic metastases and a histologically confirmed brain metastasis. Although the contributions of tumor biology and individual treatments cannot be established, the clinical course highlights the heterogeneity of metastatic TNBC and the importance of individualized multidisciplinary management.

title: Lung ultrasound versus chest X-ray for detection of pneumonia in older patients: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: Purpose Pneumonia in older people is often difficult to diagnose due to atypical presentations and limitations of chest X-ray, which can be affected by poor inspiratory effort, immobility, and chronic comorbidities. Lung ultrasound has been proposed as a more accurate modality. This review aimed to compare the diagnostic accuracy of lung ultrasound and chest X-ray for pneumonia in older patients. Methods A comprehensive search of PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library, supplemented by backward citation tracing, identified studies evaluating both lung ultrasound and chest X-ray in patients aged ≥60 years. Risk of bias was assessed with QUADAS-2. The studies were screened, selected, and reviewed by two authors who worked independently. Pooled diagnostic odds ratios (DORs) were calculated using random-effects models. Sensitivity, specificity, and AUC were pooled using a bivariate random-effects meta-analysis (BRMA). Results From 2,148 records, nine studies met inclusion criteria. Lung ultrasound consistently demonstrated higher sensitivity with comparable specificity to chest X-ray. Meta-analysis showed lung US had a superior DOR (93.35; 95% CI 27.54-316.45) compared with chest X-ray (8.33; 95% CI 3.09-22.46). BRMA estimates indicated excellent lung ultrasound performance (AUC 0.97; sensitivity 0.94; specificity 0.88), whereas chest X-ray showed lower accuracy (AUC 0.69; sensitivity 0.63; specificity 0.86). Conclusion Lung ultrasound is a rapid and radiation-free diagnostic tool that is more sensitive than chest X-ray for diagnosing pneumonia in older patients where operator expertise is available, so it should be considered as a suitable alternative or complementary imaging modality to chest X-ray to diagnose pneumonia in older patients.

title: A digital twin roadmap for adult spinal deformity.
abstract: Adult spinal deformity (ASD) surgery is a high-risk, high-cost domain in which preoperative planning plays a critical role in determining alignment goals, surgical strategy, and the balance between deformity correction and treatment-related complications, yet decisions still rely heavily on static radiographs, classification systems, and surgeon experience. In parallel, medical digital twins, continuously updated, patient-specific computational models that simulate alternative treatment paths, are emerging in other medical disciplines but have not been formally articulated for ASD. In this narrative review, we adapt the recently proposed five-component medical digital twin framework (patient, data connection, patient-in-silico, interface, and synchronization policy) to adult spinal deformity by mapping each component to ASD-specific data sources, computational models, clinical workflows, and validation pathways. We outline how existing tools in ASD, including classification systems, frailty and bone-health metrics, biomechanical modeling, motion analysis, mobile health data, and machine learning risk calculators, can serve as inputs to an ASD digital twin. We highlight priority use cases, such as choosing the magnitude of surgery, bone-health-aware planning, pelvic fixation and rod strategy, and selection among open, hybrid, and minimally invasive approaches, all reframed as comparative simulations with explicit uncertainty bands. Finally, we propose a staged roadmap, from minimal viable twins evaluated via retrospective replay, to shadow-mode deployment, to oversighted clinical pilots, while detailing challenges in data harmonization, model validity, governance, and equity. Rather than claiming that a mature ASD digital twin exists today, this work offers a practical blueprint for how digital twins could evolve into auditable, patient-specific decision-support tools that augment, rather than replace, surgeon judgment in spinal deformity surgery.

title: Determination of total free acids in UiO-66 via extraction-decoupled gas-evolvement headspace detection.
abstract: The accurate quantification of free acidic species occluded within metal-organic frameworks (i.e., UiO-66) is essential for evaluating synthesis completeness, material purity, and post-synthetic processing. In this work, a rapid and automated headspace gas chromatography (HS‑GC) method was developed for the determination of total free acids in MOFs. The strategy couples ultrasound‑assisted methanolic extraction with a selective phase‑conversion reaction: the extracted carboxylic acids react stoichiometrically with bicarbonate in a sealed headspace vial to liberate carbon dioxide, which is then detected by HS‑GC. Under systematically optimized conditions, the method exhibited excellent linearity, high sensitivity with a low limit of detection, and satisfactory precision. Accuracy was confirmed by near‑quantitative spike recoveries and by close agreement with a well‑established spectrophotometric reference method. Leveraging the automated headspace platform, the procedure substantially reduced sample cycle time and enabled high‑throughput operation while markedly decreasing organic solvent consumption relative to conventional wet‑chemical protocols. This approach provides a reliable, efficient, and environmentally favorable tool for routine monitoring of free acid content in MOFs (i.e., UiO-66), facilitating quality control in both laboratory‑scale research and scaled‑up synthesis.

title: AI-derived cardiothoracic structures and coronary artery calcification volumes on non-contrast CT as predictors of mortality in pulmonary hypertension.
abstract: Objective To assess the prognostic value of AI-derived cardiothoracic structures and coronary artery calcification volumetric measurements in pulmonary hypertension (PH) using non-gated, non-contrast CT. Materials and methods Patients with suspected PH who underwent non-gated, non-contrast chest CT and right heart catheterisation within one month were retrospectively identified from the Assessing the Spectrum of PH Identified at a Referral Centre (ASPIRE) registry. Two validated deep learning models were used to segment and measure the volumes of cardiothoracic structures and coronary artery calcifications. The prognostic value of AI-derived cardiothoracic structures and coronary artery calcification volumetric measurements was assessed using univariable and multivariable Cox regression adjusted for demographics and PH subgroups and REVEAL scores. Results Six hundred twenty patients were included (mean age 64 ± 13 years; 62% female; 388 patients died during follow-up), comprising 202 patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension, 84 with PH-LHD, 112 with PH associated with lung disease, 65 with chronic thromboembolic PH, 9 with unclear PH, and 148 patients without PH. Calcifications were present in the right coronary artery (RCA), mainstem and left anterior descending artery (LAD), and left circumflex artery (LCX) in 45%, 67%, and 35% of patients, respectively. In multivariable Cox regression analysis adjusted for age, sex, and PH subgroup, right atrial (RA) volume was independently associated with mortality (HR 1.024, 95% CI: 1.009-1.039, p = 0.001), as were coronary artery calcifications in the RCA (HR 1.378, 95% CI: 1.113-1.705, p = 0.003), mainstem and LAD (HR 1.868, 95% CI: 1.441-2.421, p < 0.001), and LCX (HR 1.342, 95% CI: 1.084-1.660, p = 0.007). After further adjustment for the REVEAL risk score, these associations remained significant (RA volume HR 1.026, RCA calcification HR 1.604, mainstem and LAD calcification HR 2.339, LCX calcification HR 1.576; all p < 0.001). Conclusion AI-derived RA volume and coronary artery calcifications are independently associated with increased mortality in PH patients. Key points Question The prognostic significance of AI-derived cardiothoracic volumes and coronary artery calcification measured on routine non-gated, non-contrast chest CT in patients with PH remains uncertain. Findings AI-derived RA volume and coronary artery calcification volumes independently predicted mortality in PH patients, even after adjustment for demographics, PH subgroups, and REVEAL score. Relevance statement Automated CT-based AI measurements can provide additional prognostic biomarkers to improve risk stratification in PH beyond established clinical scores. Graphical abstract

title: Level-specific morphometry of the cervical laminae and zygapophysial joints for posterior laminoforaminotomy: a combined computed tomography, magnetic resonance imaging and anatomical donor study.
abstract: Background Posterior cervical laminoforaminotomy passes between the laminae and the medial zygapophysial (facet) joints, where safe bone removal is measured in millimeters. The poor depiction of cortical bone on conventional magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is well known, but its size relative to computed tomography (CT) has not been quantified for each dimension and level. Methods Fifty adults (25 women, 25 men; mean age 48.1±14.4 years) with routine cervical CT and MRI within 30 days were studied. One observer measured laminar, facet joint and articular process dimensions bilaterally from C2 to C7; agreement was assessed with intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC). Eight fresh-frozen anatomical donors were dissected and measured as a separate anatomical reference. Results MRI values were lower than CT values for articular process thickness at every joint (by 0.9-1.7mm) and for lamina thickness at most levels (by up to 1.2mm at C2; C4 excepted). Agreement was poor to moderate for every parameter (ICC 0.001-0.71), highest for lamina height and facet joint length. Half of the mean CT facet joint length was 4.9-5.4mm at each joint, 4.2-5.0mm in women, and an estimated 2.4-2.6mm at the 5th percentile at C7-T1. Lamina height and facet joint length were greater in men at all levels. Conclusions Routine CT and MRI measurements are not interchangeable in the individual patient, and dimensions that set drilling depth and facetectomy extent are better taken from CT. The 5-mm value is half of a mean dimension, not a validated safe resection distance or an operative target.

title: Imaging Subphenotypes in Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome: From Characterization to Treatment-Effect Modification.
abstract: Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) is defined by clinical and radiographic criteria, yet patients differ in underlying biology, physiological impairment, and regional lung injury. Such heterogeneity may influence treatment response. Current ventilatory strategies, however, are generally guided by physiological targets without fully accounting for the biological, structural, and functional diversity of ARDS. Computed tomography, lung ultrasound, and electrical impedance tomography offer complementary information on lung morphology, aeration, and regional ventilation, while selected approaches may inform recruitability assessment. Nevertheless, evidence that imaging-defined subphenotypes identify patients who derive differential clinical benefit from specific interventions remains limited. This review examines the contribution of lung imaging to individualized respiratory management in ARDS, separating descriptive and prognostic findings from evidence of treatment-effect modification. Limitations of categorical classification and the dynamic nature of lung injury are discussed alongside the potential integration of imaging, physiological, biological, and clinical data. Such multimodal approaches remain investigational but may support evaluation of heterogeneous responses to positive end-expiratory pressure, prone positioning, and other supportive strategies. Before these approaches can guide treatment selection, standardized image acquisition, reproducible classification, longitudinal assessment, independent validation, and prospective demonstration of clinical benefit are required.

title: Deep Learning-Based Gadolinium-Free Virtual Contrast-Enhanced MRI for Predicting Immediate HIFU Ablation Outcomes in Uterine Fibroids.
abstract: Rationale and objectives Accurate assessment of microvascular perfusion is essential for predicting high-intensity focused ultrasound (HIFU) ablation outcomes in uterine fibroids. Contrast-enhanced T1-weighted imaging (CE-T1WI) is widely used for vascular evaluation; however, gadolinium-based agents pose safety concerns and may interfere with temperature monitoring. This study aimed to generate synthetic CE-T1WI (Syn-CE-T1WI) from T2-weighted imaging (T2WI) using deep learning for predicting immediate HIFU ablation outcomes. Materials and methods A mask-guided 3D conditional generative adversarial network (3D-cGAN) was developed using magnetic resonance imaging data from 300 patients (240 training, 60 testing). Syn-CE-T1WI was generated from T2WI. Image quality was assessed using peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR), structural similarity index (SSIM), and mean absolute error (MAE). Three radiologists performed blinded evaluations of image authenticity and quality. A binary classification task was used to compare Syn-CE-T1WI and Real-CE-T1WI for predicting HIFU outcomes. Results In the test set, PSNR was 27.05 ± 2.21 dB, SSIM was 0.825 ± 0.12, and MAE was 0.023. Radiologists achieved a mean accuracy of 52.8% in distinguishing real from synthetic images (all P > 0.05). Overall, 88.9% of Syn-CE-T1WI were rated clinically acceptable. For outcome prediction, Syn-CE-T1WI achieved areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs) of 0.713-0.763, comparable to Real-CE-T1WI (0.725-0.775; all P > 0.05). Combining Syn-CE-T1WI with T2WI yielded AUCs of 0.775-0.800, numerically higher than T2WI alone (0.713-0.763), and similar to T2WI + Real-CE-T1WI (0.800-0.813; all P > 0.05). Conclusion The mask-guided 3D-cGAN enabled the generation of high-fidelity, gadolinium-free Syn-CE-T1WI that may support noninvasive prediction of immediate HIFU ablation outcomes in uterine fibroids.

title: Noninvasive Prediction of Tumor Malignancy Grade in Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma with Dual-Energy CT: A Novel Index Integrating Histopathological Differentiation and Ki-67.
abstract: Rationale and objectives To preliminarily develop and validate an integrated model based on clinical features and rapid-kVp-switching dual-energy CT (DECT) 3D volumetric parameters for the noninvasive prediction of a novel Grade of Malignancy (GOM) in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC)-a composite index integrating histopathological differentiation and Ki-67 index. Materials and methods This retrospective study enrolled 183 patients with pathologically confirmed PDAC. Patients were randomly allocated into training (n=128) and validation (n=55) cohorts. From the portal venous phase scans, three quantitative 3D volumetric parameters were extracted from the tumor volume: iodine concentration (IC), the slope of the spectral attenuation curve, and effective atomic number. Independent predictors for the GOM were identified through univariate and multivariate logistic regression analysis. The discriminatory performance of the developed models was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic curve analysis, and clinical utility was assessed with decision curve analysis. Results The integrated model, which combined the DECT parameter (3D VOI-IC) and CA125, demonstrated superior predictive performance compared to models using clinical or DECT features alone. In the training cohort, the integrated model achieved an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.821 (95% CI: 0.743-0.899), which was robustly validated with an AUC of 0.806 (95% CI: 0.684-0.928) in the validation cohort. Decision curve analysis confirmed that this combined model provided the highest clinical net benefit across a wide range of threshold probabilities. Conclusion Our findings suggest that an integrated model incorporating the 3D volumetric parameter IC from DECT and CA125 could be a useful and noninvasive adjunct for preoperative prediction of the comprehensive GOM in PDAC, though further validation is needed.

title: High-Frequency Ultrasound Combined with Percutaneous Lymphatic Contrast-Enhanced Ultrasound for Preoperative Localization of Lymphaticovenous Anastomosis in Perineal Lymphedema.
abstract: Rationale and objectives Lymphaticovenous anastomosis (LVA) is an effective surgical procedure for perineal lymphedema by reconstructing lymphatic pathways. The success of LVA highly depends on accurate preoperative identification and localization of functional lymphatic vessels and corresponding superficial venules. This study aimed to assess the feasibility of high-frequency ultrasound (HFUS) combined with percutaneous lymphatic contrast-enhanced ultrasound (PL-CEUS) for identifying the optimal anastomotic site for LVA surgery in patients with perineal lymphedema. title: Integrating Intratumoral and Peritumoral Features via a Cross-Attention Transformer on Super-resolution MRI for Glioblastoma Survival Risk Stratification: A Multicenter Study.
abstract: Rationale and objectives To develop and validate a Cross-Region Transformer using super-resolution (SR) magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) to integrate intratumoral and peritumoral features for overall survival (OS) prediction in glioblastoma. Materials and methods This multicenter study included 362 patients (training, n = 228; internal test, n = 57; external validation, n = 77). Preoperative contrast-enhanced T1-weighted and T2-weighted MRI underwent generative adversarial network-based SR reconstruction. Intratumoral and 10-mm peritumoral features were extracted using 2.5D convolutional neural networks and fused by asymmetric cross-attention to generate a deep learning-based risk score (DLRS), which was combined with independent clinical factors. Performance was evaluated using C-index, time-dependent receiver operating characteristic analysis, calibration, decision curve analysis, Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping, and SHapley Additive exPlanations. Results The Cross-Region Transformer achieved C-indices of 0.787 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.734-0.840), 0.711 (95% CI, 0.593-0.829), and 0.726 (95% CI, 0.627-0.826) in the training, internal test, and external validation cohorts, respectively, with numerically higher discrimination than single-region and feature-concatenation models. The combined clinical-DLRS model, incorporating the Stupp regimen, number of lesions, Ki-67 index, and DLRS, achieved corresponding C-indices of 0.836 (95% CI, 0.788-0.884), 0.742 (95% CI, 0.628-0.855), and 0.754 (95% CI, 0.658-0.850). The DLRS significantly stratified OS in external validation (median, 7.5 vs 23.5 months; P < 0.001). Interpretability analyses highlighted enhancing margins within the necrotic core and the intratumoral-peritumoral interface. Conclusion The Cross-Region Transformer integrates complementary intratumoral and peritumoral representations from SR MRI. The resulting interpretable DLRS supports noninvasive survival prediction and risk stratification in glioblastoma.

title: Automatic Ultrasound Habitat Radiomics for Differentiating Henoch-Schonlein Purpura Nephritis from IgA Nephropathy in Children: A Multicenter Study.
abstract: Rationale and objectives To assess a noninvasive ultrasound habitat radiomics approach with automatic kidney segmentation for distinguishing pediatric Henoch-Schonlein purpura nephritis (HSPN) from immunoglobulin A nephropathy (IgAN). Materials and methods This retrospective multicenter study included 592 biopsy-confirmed pediatric patients from three centers (HSPN, n = 338; IgAN, n = 254). The development cohort (n = 453) was split into training (n = 362) and internal validation (n = 91) cohorts, and an independent external validation cohort (n = 139) was used for final testing. Kidney regions of interest were automatically segmented using nnU-Net. K-means clustering defined three echogenic habitat subregions, and 408 radiomics features were extracted from the whole-kidney region and habitat subregions. Feature selection was performed in the training cohort, and three machine-learning classifiers were evaluated. The selected radiomics model was compared with clinical and combined models. Results nnU-Net achieved high kidney segmentation performance, with a mean Dice similarity coefficient of 0.957 and a mean intersection over union of 0.918 in the independent healthy-child test set. Fifteen radiomics features were retained, including six whole-kidney features and nine habitat-derived features. Logistic regression showed stable performance, with areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs) of 0.806 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.715-0.897) internally and 0.825 (95% CI, 0.758-0.892) externally. The combined model outperformed the clinical model in AUC in both cohorts (0.846 vs 0.717; 0.805 vs 0.733). Conclusion This deep-learning-assisted ultrasound habitat radiomics approach enabled automatic kidney delineation and showed encouraging performance as a reproducible imaging adjunct for differentiating pediatric HSPN from IgAN.
