title: Psoas muscle index as a prognostic indicator in acute cholangitis.
abstract: Acute cholangitis is associated with substantial short-term mortality, particularly among elderly and comorbid patients. Conventional severity scores emphasize acute organ dysfunction but may inadequately capture underlying physiological reserve. We evaluated the prognostic value of the psoas muscle index (PMI), a computed tomography (CT)-derived measure of skeletal muscle mass, in patients hospitalized with acute cholangitis. We analyzed 457 adults with acute cholangitis admitted to Emek Medical Center. PMI (cm²/m²) was measured on abdominal CT at the L3 level. Primary outcomes were 30-day and 90-day all-cause mortality. Secondary outcomes included prolonged length of stay (> 5 days) and a composite complication endpoint, defined as sepsis or septic shock, mechanical ventilation, or acute kidney injury. Multivariate logistic regression models were simplified and adjusted for clinically selected covariates, including age, sex, body mass index (BMI), chronic renal failure, chronic heart failure, albumin, and white blood cell count. Missing covariates were handled using multiple imputations, and complete-case analysis was performed as a sensitivity analysis. Exploratory generalized linear model tree analyses were used to assess heterogeneity in the association between PMI and selected clinical outcomes. The final cohort included 457 patients. Thirty-day and 90-day mortality occurred in 55 (12.0%) and 74 (16.2%) patients, respectively. Patients who died within 90 days had lower PMI than survivors (median 3.81 vs. 4.89 cm²/m²; P < 0.001). In the revised multivariate models, higher PMI was associated with lower odds of 30-day mortality [odds ratio (OR) = 0.63, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.46-0.85; P = 0.003], 90-day mortality (OR = 0.58, 95% CI: 0.44-0.76; P < 0.001), and the composite complication endpoint (OR = 0.74, 95% CI: 0.58-0.93; P = 0.015). PMI was not significantly associated with prolonged hospitalization (OR = 0.92, 95% CI: 0.80-1.05; P = 0.200). Complete-case analysis for 90-day mortality yielded similar results (OR = 0.54, 95% CI: 0.38-0.75; P < 0.001). Exploratory generalized linear model (GLM) tree analyses suggested that the association between PMI and 90-day mortality was most evident among patients with moderately reduced albumin levels, while the association with the composite complication endpoint was most pronounced among patients with chronic renal failure and lower inflammatory burden. Lower CT-derived PMI was associated with increased short-term mortality and severe in-hospital complications in patients with acute cholangitis. PMI should be interpreted as an opportunistic imaging-based prognostic marker that reflects reduced physiological reserve, rather than as evidence of a causal relationship. Prospective validation incorporating functional frailty and nutritional measures is warranted.
originalAbstract: Acute cholangitis is associated with substantial short-term mortality, particularly among elderly and comorbid patients. Conventional severity scores emphasize acute organ dysfunction but may inadequately capture underlying physiological reserve. We evaluated the prognostic value of the psoas muscle index (PMI), a computed tomography (CT)-derived measure of skeletal muscle mass, in patients hospitalized with acute cholangitis. We analyzed 457 adults with acute cholangitis admitted to Emek Medical Center. PMI (cm²/m²) was measured on abdominal CT at the L3 level. Primary outcomes were 30-day and 90-day all-cause mortality. Secondary outcomes included prolonged length of stay (> 5 days) and a composite complication endpoint, defined as sepsis or septic shock, mechanical ventilation, or acute kidney injury. Multivariate logistic regression models were simplified and adjusted for clinically selected covariates, including age, sex, body mass index (BMI), chronic renal failure, chronic heart failure, albumin, and white blood cell count. Missing covariates were handled using multiple imputations, and complete-case analysis was performed as a sensitivity analysis. Exploratory generalized linear model tree analyses were used to assess heterogeneity in the association between PMI and selected clinical outcomes. The final cohort included 457 patients. Thirty-day and 90-day mortality occurred in 55 (12.0%) and 74 (16.2%) patients, respectively. Patients who died within 90 days had lower PMI than survivors (median 3.81 vs. 4.89 cm²/m²; P < 0.001). In the revised multivariate models, higher PMI was associated with lower odds of 30-day mortality [odds ratio (OR) = 0.63, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.46-0.85; P = 0.003], 90-day mortality (OR = 0.58, 95% CI: 0.44-0.76; P < 0.001), and the composite complication endpoint (OR = 0.74, 95% CI: 0.58-0.93; P = 0.015). PMI was not significantly associated with prolonged hospitalization (OR = 0.92, 95% CI: 0.80-1.05; P = 0.200). Complete-case analysis for 90-day mortality yielded similar results (OR = 0.54, 95% CI: 0.38-0.75; P < 0.001). Exploratory generalized linear model (GLM) tree analyses suggested that the association between PMI and 90-day mortality was most evident among patients with moderately reduced albumin levels, while the association with the composite complication endpoint was most pronounced among patients with chronic renal failure and lower inflammatory burden. Lower CT-derived PMI was associated with increased short-term mortality and severe in-hospital complications in patients with acute cholangitis. PMI should be interpreted as an opportunistic imaging-based prognostic marker that reflects reduced physiological reserve, rather than as evidence of a causal relationship. Prospective validation incorporating functional frailty and nutritional measures is warranted.

title: Clinical Characteristics and 2-Year Follow-Up of Patients With Takayasu Arteritis and Pulmonary Artery Involvement.
abstract: The frequency of pulmonary arterial (PA) involvement (PAI) in Takayasu arteritis (TAK) has been reported to range from 14.0% to 57.0%. PAI may be associated with a worse prognosis; therefore, early detection and treatment of PAI may improve the disease course. This study assessed the characteristics and follow-up of TAK patients with PAI. Seventy-two TAK patients (62 female, 10 male) who underwent computed tomography pulmonary angiography (CTPA) to investigate PAI were included. A radiologist reviewed CTPA images, and PAI was characterised by increased pulmonary artery wall thickness, stenosis, and/or thrombosis. The mean age was 46.4±13.0 years, and nine patients had active disease. The treatments for TAK were immunosuppressives (IS) in 62 (86.1%), biological treatment in 25 (34.7%), glucocorticoids (GCs) in 30 (41.7%), and acetylsalicylic acid (ASA) in 50 (69.4%) patients. Twenty-two (30.6%) patients had pulmonary symptoms, most commonly dyspnoea and chest pain. PAI was detected in 13 (18.1%) patients, and PA thrombosis unrelated to vasculitis was present in five (6.9%) patients. Among PAI patients, IS treatment was changed in nine (69.2%), GC dose was increased in eight (61.5%), and anticoagulants were started in seven (53.8%). Pulmonary symptoms (92.3% vs 16.9%), C-reactive protein (CRP) (25.8 vs 4.0 mg/L), and erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) (34.5 vs 16.2 mm/h) values were significantly higher in patients with PAI (p<0.001, p=0.001, p=0.008). PAI was significantly lower in patients using ASA (30.8% vs 69.2%) (p=0.002). After 2 years of follow-up, one patient with PAI had a relapse of TAK and three patients had chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension. PAI was present in 18.1% of TAK patients, and pulmonary symptoms, higher ESR and CRP values, and less frequent ASA use were associated with PAI.

title: Prognostic Value of Late Gadolinium Enhancement in Non-Ischemic Dilated Cardiomyopathy: A Prospective Observational Study from India.
abstract: Background Non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy (NIDCM) represents a significant cause of heart failure and sudden cardiac death (SCD). Current risk stratification relies heavily on left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), which has limitations in predicting adverse outcomes. Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) on cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) imaging may provide additional prognostic information. Methods This prospective observational study enrolled 88 consecutive NIDCM patients who underwent CMR imaging at our institution. Patients were followed for a minimum of 6 months and thereafter until a common study closure date, giving a mean follow-up of 337±173 days. The primary endpoint was a composite of major adverse cardiac events (MACE), defined as sudden cardiac death, heart failure death, aborted sudden cardiac death, sustained ventricular tachycardia, and heart failure hospitalization. Results LGE was present in 44 patients (50%). The most common pattern was mid-myocardial enhancement (40.9%), followed by a combination of patterns (25.0%) and transmural enhancement (22.7%); the interventricular septum was the most frequently involved segment (81.8%). MACE occurred in 22.7% of LGE-positive patients versus 13.6% of LGE-negative patients. ROC curve analysis identified LGE extent >26% of LV volume as the optimal threshold for predicting MACE (sensitivity 70%, specificity 73.5%, AUC 0.75). Patients with LGE >26% had significantly higher event rates (43.7% vs 10.7%; unadjusted OR 6.48, 95% CI 1.45-28.9; p=0.02). Conclusions Greater LGE extent was associated with adverse cardiac events in NIDCM patients. CMR-based risk stratification may help identify high-risk patients who could benefit from ICD, but external validation in larger cohorts is required before using this threshold clinically.

title: Electron-beam-crosslinked injectable poly-γ-glutamic acid hydrogels: Physicochemical properties, long-term in vivo retention, and biocompatibility.
abstract: Injectable hydrogels for biomedical applications require controllable mechanical properties, sustained in vivo retention, and favorable biocompatibility. Here, injectable poly-γ-glutamic acid (γ-PGA) hydrogels were prepared by electron-beam (EB) irradiation at 30 kGy (low dose, LD), 150 kGy (medium dose, MD), and 200 kGy (high dose, HD), without additional chemical crosslinking agents. Nuclear magnetic resonance and Fourier-transform infrared analyses revealed irradiation-induced spectral changes in γ-PGA. Physicochemical and mechanical characterization demonstrated distinct differences in swelling behavior, gel fraction, rheological properties, and injection force among the irradiation groups. In vivo retention and biocompatibility were assessed in mice over 180 days following subcutaneous injection. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-based volumetric analysis showed progressively prolonged retention from LD to HD, with γ-PGA (LD) remaining detectable through day 7, γ-PGA (MD) through day 150, and γ-PGA (HD) retaining 74.26 ± 3.77% of its initial volume on day 180. Higher irradiation levels were also associated with greater G' and G″ values and reduced maximum swelling. Compared with the hyaluronic acid hydrogel, the γ-PGA hydrogels exhibited less pronounced early post-injection volume expansion, while their long-term MRI-detectable volume profiles varied among the irradiation groups. No marked local or systemic adverse responses were detected based on MRI, histological observations, serum cytokine analysis, hematologic assessment, body weight monitoring, and relative organ weight measurements. Overall, EB irradiation enabled the preparation of injectable γ-PGA hydrogels with irradiation-dependent physicochemical and rheological properties, prolonged in vivo retention, practical injectability, and favorable biocompatibility.

title: Silent brain infarction and clinical outcomes in rheumatic mitral stenosis: A prospective cohort study.
abstract: Background Rheumatic mitral stenosis (MS) affects a relatively young population. Thromboembolic risk in MS is traditionally attributed to atrial fibrillation (AF), although silent brain infarction (SBI) may occur in sinus rhythm. Further, the contribution of underlying atrial disease independent of rhythm remains uncertain. Objectives To determine the prevalence and correlates of SBI and evaluate associations with subsequent cerebrovascular and clinical outcomes. Methods In this prospective cohort, 211 adults with moderate-to-severe rheumatic MS underwent baseline brain MRI, echocardiography, biomarker assessment, and rhythm evaluation. Firth penalized logistic regression was used for SBI and longitudinal outcomes. Clinical follow-up was available in 194 patients. Results SBI was present in 44 patients (20.9%). SBI occurred in 25.4% with AF and 18.6% in sinus rhythm (unadjusted OR 1.49, 95% CI 0.70-3.10; p = 0.284); adjusted AF was not significantly associated with SBI (OR 0.82, 95% CI 0.37-1.76; p = 0.605). Each doubling of BNP was associated with SBI overall (OR 1.34, 95% CI 1.01-1.82; p = 0.040) and in sinus rhythm (OR 1.56, 95% CI 1.12-2.27; p = 0.007). During follow-up, 15 patients developed stroke/TIA; baseline SBI was associated with subsequent stroke/TIA (17.1% vs 5.2%; adjusted OR 3.40, 95% CI 1.14-9.96; p = 0.029). BNP was associated with stroke/death (49 events; OR per doubling 1.45, 95% CI 1.09-2.00; p = 0.010) and death (40 events; OR 1.57, 95% CI 1.14-2.25; p = 0.005), but not stroke/TIA. Conclusions SBI is common in rheumatic MS and identifies patients at higher subsequent cerebrovascular risk. BNP is associated with SBI and broader adverse prognosis, particularly mortality. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require further validation.

title: Pleural empyema and perisplenic abscess caused by Clostridioides difficile in a patient with liver cirrhosis and previous C. difficile colitis: a case report.
abstract: Background Clostridioides difficile is a leading cause of healthcare-associated diarrhea, whereas extraintestinal infection is rare and pleural involvement is exceptional, with only a handful of cases reported to date. Patients with liver cirrhosis are at increased risk of bacterial infection and of C. difficile infection, but C. difficile pleural empyema has been reported only once in this population. Case presentation A 43-year-old man with alcohol-related liver cirrhosis (Child-Pugh class C) and C. difficile colitis two years earlier was admitted with hepatic decompensation and a C-reactive protein of 151 mg/L, without gastrointestinal symptoms. Computed tomography showed a large left-sided pleural collection. The aspirate contained 6,870 cells/µL with 94.2% granulocytes and had a pH of 6.97, consistent with empyema. Piperacillin/tazobactam was started empirically and empyemectomy was performed. Intraoperative swabs yielded C. difficile on MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry and toxin PCR was positive; histopathology showed acute purulent pleuritis. Two weeks later the empyema recurred and a new perisplenic collection appeared; C. difficile toxin was again detected at both sites. Treatment was escalated to meropenem, vancomycin and metronidazole, combined with repeat surgical evacuation and percutaneous drainage. Repeated stool testing for C. difficile antigen and toxin remained negative. After a prolonged intensive care stay requiring tracheostomy, the patient recovered and was discharged to a rehabilitation facility. Conclusions C. difficile should be considered as a cause of pleural empyema, particularly in patients with liver cirrhosis and previous C. difficile infection. Recovery of C. difficile from extraintestinal specimens should not be dismissed as contamination; timely source control combined with targeted antimicrobial therapy is essential for a favorable outcome.

title: Artificial intelligence for detecting C-shaped canals on dental radiographs: A systematic review and bayesian diagnostic accuracy meta-analysis.
abstract: Objective To evaluate AI-based identification of C-shaped canals across dental radiographic modalities, with an exploratory synthesis of conventional panoramic detection using cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) reference labels. Methods Seven sources were searched through August 12, 2026. Peer-reviewed original studies were appraised using QUADAS-3, STARD-AI, and GRADE. Binary panoramic estimates with CBCT reference and auditable counts were pooled using a Bayesian bivariate model nesting external centers within parent studies. Prospero CRD420251046384. Results Nine studies were included; three independent parent studies supplied five cohorts (899C-shaped and 953 non-C-shaped teeth). Pooled sensitivity was 0.918 (95 % credible interval [CrI], 0.837-0.962) and specificity 0.885 (0.588-0.969). Marginal model-implied new-parent-study prediction intervals were 0.716-0.981 and 0.219-0.993, respectively. Only one program provided multicenter external evaluation, with center-specific optimized thresholds. All selected estimates had high risk of bias. Certainty was low for sensitivity and very low for specificity. Conclusions The sparse evidence does not establish dependable clinical performance. Predictive uncertainty and workflow limitations constrain transportability. Prospective evaluation of prespecified systems and clinical consequences is needed before implementation.

Prospero

title: Clinical utility of computed tomography angiography in assessing internal maxillary artery position during temporomandibular joint ankylosis surgery.
abstract: Temporomandibular joint (TMJ) ankylosis surgery carries a high risk of intraoperative bleeding due to the close anatomical relationship between the ankylotic mass and the internal maxillary artery (IMA). Although computed tomography angiography (CTA) is widely used for preoperative vascular assessment, its reliability in predicting the intraoperative IMA course in TMJ ankylosis surgery remains uncertain. This exploratory prospective case series included 34 patients (22 males, 12 females; mean age 19.6 ± 2.5 years) with TMJ ankylosis involving 48 joints treated with 1 cm gap arthroplasty. CTA identified three IMA-ankylotic mass relationships: close contact (n = 20, further subdivided into medial, n = 8; posterior, n = 12), enclosed (n = 13), and no contact (n = 15). Overall concordance between preoperative CTA-based IMA classification and intraoperative findings was 56.3%, with discordance in 43.7% of joints (Cramér's V = 0.069; P = 0.97). Concordance varied across CTA categories, with the lowest concordance observed in the no contact group (53.3%). Despite differences in preoperative CTA-based IMA classification, intraoperative outcomes did not differ significantly among groups. Ankylotic mass resection time was comparable across categories (median 23-24 min; P = 0.085), and no significant differences were observed in estimated blood loss, vascular control measures, or blood transfusion requirements. In conclusion, CTA demonstrates limited concordance with the clinically observed intraoperative course of the IMA in TMJ ankylosis surgery and does not significantly stratify intraoperative outcomes. Therefore, it may be considered a complementary tool for preoperative planning rather than a definitive predictor of intraoperative vascular anatomy.

title: Classification and surgical treatment of temporomandibular joint calcium pyrophosphate deposition disease: a single-center case series.
abstract: This study aimed to classify calcium pyrophosphate deposition disease of the temporomandibular joint and evaluate the therapeutic outcomes. Surgically treated patients from January 2020 to September 2025 were classified into three types based on lesion location and extent. Type I involved the superior compartment with or without skull base destruction. Type II affected the inferior compartment with or without condylar destruction. Type III involved both compartments affecting the condyle and skull base. Treatments included complete excision and reconstruction using autologous or alloplastic materials. Maximum interincisal opening and visual analogue scale pain scores were evaluated preoperatively and at follow-ups of at least 6 months, while computed tomography assessed recurrence and reconstruction. Ten patients (mean age of 57.2 years) were included, comprising four in type I, four in type II, and two in type III. Bone invasion occurred in eight patients. Reconstruction procedures involved autologous tissues, such as temporalis myofascial flaps or coronoid grafts in three patients, and alloplastic materials in five. The mean follow-up duration was 25.1 months. Maximum (range) interincisal opening was improved from 33.0 mm (23.0-48.0) to 39.5 mm (37.0-45.0) (P < 0.05). Pain scores decreased from 6.0 (2.0-8.0) to 0.0 (0.0-1.0) (P < 0.05). One patient had coronoid process graft resorption without malocclusion. No recurrence, screw loosening, or implant displacement occurred. TMJ CPPD can be classified and treated according to the lesion location and extension. Complete excision and reconstruction are associated with low recurrence.

title: Sivan TMJ-OPMS classification based on dual-mode rendering three-dimensional cone-beam computed tomography technique for the diagnosis of temporomandibular joint disorders.
abstract: This study aimed to develop and validate the Sivan TMJ-OPMS classification using three-dimensional (3D) dual-mode cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) rendering to integrate osseous changes (O), disc position (P), disc morphology (M), and joint space (S) for standardized phenotyping and severity stratification of temporomandibular disorders (TMDs). A retrospective evaluation included 132 patients (264 joints), assessed using dual-mode 3D CBCT datasets. OPMS parameters were defined using novel anatomical markers: anterior and posterior condylar slopes, anterior sloping zone, and condyle-fossa axis line. Following structured training, 15 blinded raters classified anonymized images. Inter- and intra-rater reliability were assessed using Fleiss's and Cohen's kappa, and four independent raters evaluated external reproducibility. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) served as the reference standard for comparative validation. Reliability was near perfect (κ = 0.88-0.94; agreement ≈93-95%), with high external reproducibility. MRI-referenced receiver operating characteristic analysis demonstrated strong diagnostic performance (area under the curve = 0.94). Confirmatory factor analysis supported OPMS as a unified classification construct (comparative fit index/Tucker-Lewis index ≥0.95; root mean square error of approximation ≤0.06). Path analysis identified a sequential association in which osseous changes predicted disc position (β = 0.820, R² = 0.967), which influenced disc morphology (β = 0.448) and subsequently joint-space alterations (β = 0.720). Mediation analysis identified disc displacement as the intermediate link between osseous dysmorphology and joint-space pathology. This reproducible, MRI-validated, anatomically grounded CBCT-based classification offers a structured framework for TMD assessment, potentially facilitating more individualized clinical evaluation, disease severity characterization, and personalized treatment planning.

title: TTA-MVUM: A Tumor and Text-Aware Multi-View Mamba Framework for Clinical Target Volume Auto-Segmentation in Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma Radiotherapy.
abstract: Purpose Accurate segmentation of clinical target volumes (CTV) is critical for the success of radiotherapy in nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC). Manual contouring is time-consuming and prone to considerable inter-observer variability. Current auto-segmentation models rely exclusively on images, which may lead to sub-optimal accuracy. This study sought to substantially improve CTV auto-segmentation by incorporating tumor and clinical text information with multimodal deep learning. Methods and materials We retrospectively collected data from 184 NPC patients treated at our institution, with 144 cases allocated for model training and 40 for test. We propose a tumor- and text-aware multi-view UMamba (TTA-MVUM) model with text-image cross-attention modules to fuse visual and textual features. The model input comprised CT images, manually contoured primary gross tumor volume and metastatic lymph nodes, structured text contouring plan extracted by a large language model from electronic health records. Training was guided by a composite loss integrating Dice, cross-entropy and contrastive terms. Model performance was evaluated using Dice, 95% Hausdorff distance and averaged surface distance. Results The proposed TTA-MVUM model significantly outperformed state-of-the-art image-only and tumor-aware baselines, yielding mean Dice of 0.892 ± 0.035 for high-risk CTV, 0.738 ± 0.149 for low-risk CTV, and 0.889 ± 0.024 for the entire CTV, respectively, with similar improvements for other metrics. Using either tumor information or clinical text alone also surpassed baseline models, but performance remained inferior to the combined approach. Conclusions Integrating tumor priors and text guidance can substantially improve the NPC CTV auto-segmentation accuracy and clinical applicability.

title: Neoadjuvant Chemoradiotherapy with Modern Bowel-Sparing Intensity-Modulated Radiotherapy for Locally Advanced Rectal Cancer: A Multicenter Single-Arm Phase II Trial.
abstract: Purpose The study evaluated the risk of grade ≥2 acute diarrhea of modern bowel-sparing intensity-modulated radiotherapy (IMRT)-based neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy (nCRT) for locally advanced rectal cancer (LARC) versus three-dimensional conformal radiotherapy (3DCRT)-based nCRT. Materials and methods In this open-label, historically controlled, multicenter, single-arm phase II trial, patients with LARC, Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status 0-2, and adequate organ function were recruited. Protocol treatment involved concurrent capecitabine and IMRT, consisting of 45 Gy (25 fractions) for elective nodes and an optional 5.4 Gy (3 fractions) boost for gross disease. Bowel-sparing constraints included small-bowel volume receiving 15 Gy (V15Gy) of <200 cc. Acute toxicities were graded in the protocol-defined primary outcome window. Grade ≥2 acute diarrhea was tested against a 26% historical benchmark from phase II trials of 3DCRT-based nCRT with capecitabine with a one-sided α-level of 0.05 and 80% power. Results Fifty-five patients were enrolled, including 48 patients with stage III disease and 25 patients with a positive circumferential resection margin on magnetic resonance imaging. Fifty-four patients (98.2%) completed protocol-defined nCRT. The median small-bowel V15Gy was 85 cc (interquartile range, 47-105). Grade ≥2 acute diarrhea occurred in four patients (7.3%; 90% confidence interval, 2.5-15.9; p < 0.001) in the intention-to-treat cohort. Fifty patients underwent radical surgery, and the pathological complete response and circumferential resection margin >1 mm rates were 6.0% and 88.0%, respectively, with grade ≥2 postoperative complications observed in 14% of patients. After median follow-up of 14 months, the 12-month locoregional progression-free and overall survival rates were 95.0% and 98.2%, respectively. Conclusions Modern bowel-sparing IMRT in nCRT for LARC was associated with a low rate of grade ≥2 acute diarrhea with no obvious unfavorable signals for resectability, locoregional control, or safety; however, longer follow-up is needed to assess mature oncologic outcomes and late toxicities.

title: Prevalence of Muscle loss during and after Pelvic Radiotherapy in Gynecological Cancer Patients.
abstract: Introduction Women undergoing pelvic radiotherapy are at risk of developing sarcopenia, defined by muscle loss. In patients treated with radiotherapy for cervical cancer, post-treatment muscle loss has been associated with poorer cancer-specific and overall survival. This study aimed to longitudinally assess sarcopenia and changes in muscle during radiotherapy and follow-up, and to evaluate whether bioelectrical impedance analysis can serve as an accurate bedside alternative to computed tomography (CT) for sarcopenia assessment. Methods and materials This prospective cohort study included women with histologically confirmed primary cervical, endometrial, vulvar, or vaginal cancer, all scheduled to undergo external beam radiotherapy (EBRT) with curative intent. Sarcopenia was assessed at baseline, during the last week of EBRT, and at the three- and six-month follow-up. Two methods were used to evaluate sarcopenia: lumbar skeletal muscle index measured via CT scan (gold standard) and appendicular skeletal muscle mass via bioelectrical impedance analysis. Fisher's exact test and the Mann-Whitney U test were used to compare baseline characteristics between women with and without sarcopenia during the last week of radiotherapy. Results A total of 31 women were included. Based on CT scans, the prevalence of sarcopenia was 23% at baseline, 32% at the last week of radiotherapy, and 42% at the three-month follow-up. At the six-month follow-up, 29% of the women were sarcopenic. Bioelectrical impedance analysis detected sarcopenia in only 0% to 50% of cases across the various time points. Patients with FIGO stage III were significantly more frequently sarcopenic based on their appendicular skeletal muscle index as assessed by CT scan during the last week of EBRT. Conclusions The prevalence of sarcopenia is high in women treated with radiotherapy for gynecological cancer. An increase in the prevalence of sarcopenia was observed, reaching its highest point at the three-month follow-up. Sarcopenia may be underestimated when assessed using bioelectrical impedance analysis, as indicated by the low sensitivity observed.

Fisher's exact test and the Mann-Whitney U test were used to compare baseline characteristics between women with and without sarcopenia during the last week of radiotherapy.

Results

A total of 31 women were included. Based on CT scans, the prevalence of sarcopenia was 23% at baseline, 32% at the last week of radiotherapy, and 42% at the three-month follow-up. At the six-month follow-up, 29% of the women were sarcopenic. Bioelectrical impedance analysis detected sarcopenia in only 0% to 50% of cases across the various time points. Patients with FIGO stage III were significantly more frequently sarcopenic based on their appendicular skeletal muscle index as assessed by CT scan during the last week of EBRT.

Conclusions

The prevalence of sarcopenia is high in women treated with radiotherapy for gynecological cancer. An increase in the prevalence of sarcopenia was observed, reaching its highest point at the three-month follow-up. Sarcopenia may be underestimated when assessed using bioelectrical impedance analysis, as indicated by the low sensitivity observed.

title: The Complementary Impact of Amino Acid PET with Diffusion and Perfusion MRI for Glioblastoma Tumor Delineation.
abstract: Background While standard MRI imaging is known to underestimate glioblastoma tumor extent, advanced imaging techniques including 18-FDOPA PET, dynamic contrast enhanced (DCE) perfusion MRI, and diffusion weighted MRI (DWI) have been utilized on clinical trials to identify tumor within and beyond gadolinium enhancement for radiation targeting. This clinical trial analysis quantifies how DCE, DWI and 18-FDOPA PET identify tumor beyond standard imaging, and whether these techniques are complementary and feasible. Methods Patients with newly diagnosed glioblastoma enrolled on a phase II clinical trial underwent pre-radiation 18-FDOPA PET/CT, DCE, DWI, and standard MRI sequences. Tumor volumes were separately delineated using each imaging modality and incorporated into radiation target volumes, and were compared for overlapping and non-overlapping segments. Results In 153 enrolled patients included in this analysis, tumor was identified beyond conventionally used radiation volume expansions of 5-, 10-, 15-, and 20 mm from standard MRI tumor volumes in 86%, 56%, 38% and 20% of patients, respectively. Advanced imaging techniques identified partially overlapping tumor volumes; PET identified tumor outside of the advanced MRI subvolumes in 88%, while DWI and DCE identified tumor outside of standard MRI and PET in 95% cases, indicating these imaging techniques are complementary. Conclusions Advanced imaging techniques including DCE, DWI, and 18-FDOPA PET allow complementary delineation of glioblastoma beyond contrast-enhancing tumor from standard MRI, and may be most valuable when used in combination. These advanced imaging methods can potentially facilitate accurate tumor targeting with reduced CTV expansions to spare normal tissue and enable safe hypofractionated radiation therapy.

title: RESPONSE-ADAPTIVE STEREOTACTIC BODY RADIOTHERAPY BOOST AFTER CONCURRENT CHEMORADIOTHERAPY IN UNRESECTABLE STAGE III NSCLC: A PROSPECTIVE SINGLE-CENTRE COHORT STUDY.
abstract: Objective This study aimed to escalate the dose to the residual primary tumor with an adaptive stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) boost after concurrent chemoradiotherapy (CRT) in unresectable stage III non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), and to explore, within this cohort, whether a higher cumulative dose to the residual primary was associated with better locoregional control (LRC) and whether this translated into a difference in overall survival (OS). Materials and methods In this single-center, prospective, single-arm cohort, 51 patients received concurrent CRT (50 Gy/25 fractions with weekly carboplatin and paclitaxel) followed by an adaptive boost (30 Gy/5 fractions to the residual primary, 10 Gy/5 fractions to residual nodes), without consolidation durvalumab. Doses were summed by deformable registration and reported as EQD2. Response was assessed at 3 months with FDG-PET/CT (PERCIST), and toxicity with CTCAE v5.0. Outcomes estimated by Kaplan-Meier; predictors by Cox regression. Results At a median follow-up of 26 months, 2-year OS and LRC were 61.5% and 62.8%. The median PFS and DMFS were 13 and 16 months, and distant metastasis was the dominant failure pattern (41.2%). Cumulative dose below 94.77 Gy (EQD2) to the residual primary independently predicted worse LRC (HR 5.86), and a 3-month locoregional SUVmax ≥4.55 predicted worse LRC (HR 5.04). OS was independently associated with residual nodal volume, 3-month metabolic progression, and subsequent locoregional progression. Grade 3-4 pneumonitis occurred in 7.8%, grade 3 esophagitis in one patient (2%), and hemoptysis in five (9.8%). Conclusion The SBRT boost achieved encouraging locoregional control, including in bulky and node-advanced disease, without immunotherapy, and higher cumulative dose to the residual primary was associated with better locoregional control. Hemoptysis was the main safety concern and occurred predominantly in patients with pre-existing hemoptysis, supporting careful selection and strict bronchial constraints. Local escalation alone did not overcome the competing risk of distant failure.

title: Long-term preservation of normal brain tissue by minibeam radiation therapy does not require mature T cells.
abstract: Purpose Minibeam radiation therapy (MBRT) preserves normal tissue while maintaining antitumour efficacy, yet the mechanisms underlying this remarkable normal tissue tolerance remain poorly understood. Although adaptive immune responses have been implicated in the antitumour effects of spatially fractionated radiotherapy, their contribution to normal tissue preservation remains unknown. Here, we used a loss-of-function model to determine whether mature T cells are required for the expression of the long-term normal tissue-sparing phenotype associated with MBRT. Methods and materials Immunocompetent Fischer 344 rats and athymic nude rats received X-ray MBRT or conventional radiotherapy (CRT) at a mean dose of 30 Gy and were followed for up to six months. Long-term normal tissue response was assessed using complementary behavioural analyses, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), and histopathological evaluation of immune infiltration, vascular integrity, glial activation and neuronal survival. Results Nude rats developed beam-path alopecia and skin lesions earlier than immunocompetent rats and showed a transient reduction in cortical CD31 staining at 7 days post-irradiation, indicating greater acute radiosensitivity without mature T cells. Beyond this early window, the long-term phenotype was comparable between strains: no MRI-detectable lesions, no neuronal loss and no sustained glial activation at 6 months. MBRT induced modest late reductions in exploratory behaviour and recognition memory in both strains, with no significant strain × irradiation interaction. Histologically, MBRT elicited a moderate and transient CD3 + T-cell infiltration that resolved within seven days, whereas CRT induced a stronger and more sustained inflammatory response. Conclusions Mature T cells modulate the acute tissue reaction to MBRT but are not required for the long-term normal tissue-sparing phenotype. Within the sensitivity of this study, powered for large effects only, mature T cells are unlikely to be a major determinant of long-term MBRT tissue preservation, redirecting attention towards innate immune, vascular and stromal processes.

title: Intraoperative visualization with 3D fluoroscopy for posterior pelvic fixation is associated with lower cumulative imaging-related radiation exposure.
abstract: Introduction Achieving optimal screw positioning in posterior pelvic ring (PR) fracture fixation is critical for fracture stability and safety. Formerly, our institution used intraoperative plain-film fluoroscopy followed by postoperative computed tomography (CT) to assess fracture reduction and screw placement. Introduction of the 3D mobile C-arm enables immediate volumetric intraoperative assessment, may improve intraoperative visualization, and may alter conventional imaging requirements. This study compared cumulative imaging-related radiation exposure between cases performed with intraoperative 3D fluoroscopy (3DF) against standard intraoperative plain-film fluoroscopy (2DF), including postoperative CT utilization. Methods A retrospective review was conducted on patients treated for posterior PR fractures at a level 1 trauma center between 2014 and 2023. Utilization of 3DF or plain-film fluoroscopy, and any intraoperative screw changes were documented. Rates and details of postoperative complications and subsequent reoperations were recorded for patients with > 3 months follow-up. Radiation doses for 3DF, 2DF, and postoperative CT were extracted from radiology reports. Results Among 245 patients (mean age 47.2, 52.2% male) undergoing fixation for posterior PR fractures, 89 (36.3%) had 3DF intraoperatively, while 156 (63.7%) had 2DF. 27 patients (8 3DF, 19 2DF, p = 0.443) had screws changed intraoperatively, primarily to modify screw path (n = 16, 59.3%), to achieve better purchase/reduction (n = 5, 18.5%), to modify screw size (n = 3, 11.1%), to change screw type (n = 2, 7.4%), and failure to advance screw (n = 1, 3.7%). Mean radiation dose for the 3DF group was significantly lower (179.2 mGy vs 526.1 mGy, p < 0.001). When excluding postoperative CT dose (n = 194), intraoperative-only radiation remained lower with 3DF (median 79.1 (IQR 51.5-148.7) vs 318.0 (IQR 71.6-751.5) mGy; p < 0.001). Among 119 patients with > 3 months follow-up, reoperation was less frequent with 3DF (9.5% vs 31.2%, p = 0.012), predominantly for symptomatic implant removal. Discussion and conclusion Intraoperative 3DF was associated with lower cumulative radiation exposure compared to traditional fluoroscopy with routine postoperative CT, and intraoperative dose alone was also lower. Reoperation was less frequent in the 3DF group, but most reoperations were implant removals for symptomatic or planned indications. These findings highlight the potential of 3DF as a practical radiation efficient quality assurance tool in posterior pelvic fixation.

title: Machine Learning Reveals Prognostic Value of Medical History in Suspected Coronary Artery Disease.
abstract: Background Risk stratification in suspected coronary artery disease (CAD) relies on clinical history and imaging, but longitudinal medical history may provide additional prognostic information. Objectives This study evaluated whether machine learning models using 10-year historical registry data improves prediction of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) beyond demographics and stress perfusion cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) in patients with suspected CAD. Methods A total of 2,159 patients (65 ± 12 years, 44% women) undergoing stress perfusion CMR were included. Models used demographics, CMR findings, and registry diagnoses and procedures from the prior 10 years. MACE was defined as cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, or coronary intervention. Random Forest models were used for binary prediction, and Random Survival Forests (RSF) and penalized Ridge Cox regression for time-to-event analysis. Results During 2.7 ± 0.9 years of follow-up, 212 patients (9.8%) experienced MACE. For binary prediction, the area under the receiver-operating characteristic curve (AUROC) was 0.66 (95% CI: 0.62-0.69) using demographics and 0.72 (95% CI: 0.68-0.75; P = 0.001) after adding historical registry data. The full model achieved an AUROC of 0.82 (95% CI: 0.79-0.85) and outperformed the demographics-plus-CMR model (AUROC: 0.81; 95% CI: 0.78-0.84; ΔAUROC: 0.014; 95% CI: 0.002-0.027; P = 0.029). After including registry data RSF achieved a C-index of 0.81 (P = 0.144), and Cox performance decreased to C-index 0.77 (P < 0.001). Conclusions In patients with suspected CAD, machine learning models using 10-year historical registry data have the potential to improve prognostic risk prediction beyond demographics and stress perfusion CMR.

title: Fully Automated, Explainable AI Analysis of Coronary CTA Improves Prediction of Major Cardiovascular Events.
abstract: Coronary artery disease (CAD) remains a major global cause of morbidity and mortality. Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) is central to noninvasive diagnosis and risk assessment, yet current workflows are labor-intensive and depend on semiquantitative scoring systems that do not fully leverage prognostic information in CCTA. The objectives of the study were to develop and validate a fully automated, explainable artificial intelligence (AI) system (AI-automated coronary analysis [ACA]) for comprehensive CCTA analysis to predict major adverse cardiovascular events and compare its performance with conventional risk markers. AI-ACA automatically extracts a suite of CCTA-derived biomarkers, including stenosis severity, plaque burden, and composition; AI-derived CAD - reporting and data system (CAD-RADS) (AI-CADRADS); coronary tortuosity; and subtended myocardial mass, to generate interpretable risk estimates. In a retrospective cohort (n = 1,702), we compared AI-ACA with Agatston score, standard demographic risk markers, and AI-CADRADS. Model explainability was assessed using Shapley Additive Explanations. AI-ACA demonstrated higher predictive performance (area under the curve [AUC]: 0.81) than Agatston score (AUC: 0.76) and demographic markers (AUC: 0.67), and similar performance to AI-CADRADS (AUC: 0.81). AI-ACA showed better prognostic discrimination than Agatston score, reflected by a higher Harrell C-index (0.791 vs 0.742) and greater separation in event-free survival on Kaplan-Meier analysis (log-rank 31.79 vs 13.71). Shapley Additive Explanations analysis identified total plaque volume and burden, maximum stenosis severity, and AI-CADRADS as the strongest contributors to risk estimation. A fully automated and explainable AI platform for CCTA enables comprehensive quantitative characterization of CAD without manual intervention. Although prognostic performance was comparable to AI-CADRADS and modestly higher than Agatston score, the platform provides transparent biomarker-based risk assessment and scalable analysis that may facilitate broader clinical implementation of quantitative CCTA.

title: Congestion Assessed With Inferior Vena Cava Ultrasound Predicts Long-Term Outcomes in Acute Decompensated Heart Failure.
abstract: Background Inferior vena cava (IVC) parameters relate to clinical outcomes in retrospective acute decompensated heart failure (ADHF) studies, but prospective data on long-term outcomes and quality of life are unavailable. Objectives The objective of the study was to evaluate the prognostic value of IVC parameters for clinical outcomes and their association with quality of life. Methods Patients admitted for ADHF were prospectively enrolled from January 2022 to May 2024. Point-of-care IVC ultrasound was performed at admission and discharge. The Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire (KCCQ) was evaluated at baseline, 1, 6, and 12 months. The primary endpoint was the composite of all-cause mortality and ADHF rehospitalization at 12 months. Results A total of 100 patients (median age 67 years, 28% women, 45% NYHA functional class III/IV, 65% heart failure with reduced ejection fraction) were included. The primary endpoint occurred in 50 patients (9 deaths and 41 ADHF hospitalizations). In multivariable analysis, admission minimum IVC sniff diameter >1.6 cm (HR: 3.71; 95% CI: 1.97-7.01; P < 0.001), admission maximum IVC diameter >2.3 cm (HR: 2.70; 95% CI: 1.46-4.96; P = 0.001), discharge minimum IVC sniff diameter >1.3 cm (HR: 2.27; 95% CI: 1.24-4.14; P = 0.008), and discharge sniff IVC collapsibility index <36% (HR: 3.16; 95% CI: 1.64-6.06; P < 0.001) were independent predictors of the primary endpoint. KCCQ scores improved during follow-up (P time <0.001) but were not associated with the primary endpoint. Patients with admission minimum IVC sniff diameter >1.6 cm had lower KCCQ scores throughout the study period (P group = 0.03). Conclusions In ADHF patients, IVC parameters predict 12-month outcomes and may serve as objective markers to identify residual congestion and stratify risk.

title: Multiview Integration for Robust Echocardiographic Embeddings: Accessible AI for Clinical Practice.
abstract: Background Although recent artificial intelligence (AI) foundation models have shown superior performance in medical imaging, their high computational demands and reliance on large data sets limit accessibility. These issues are especially pronounced in echocardiography, where integrating complex multiview measurements for individual cases hinders AI development and clinical translation. Vector embedding approaches offer promising solutions by leveraging compact representations in AI applications. Objectives We aimed to develop a transformer-based multiview encoder that integrates multiple echocardiographic videos into unified vector embeddings and uses adversarial learning to reduce reliance on demographic shortcuts. Methods Using the MIMIC-IV-ECHO (Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV-Echocardiography) data set (7,169 studies), we trained a multiview encoder to produce study-level embeddings and evaluated them on 21 binary classification tasks covering echocardiographic measurements and clinical diagnoses. We varied adversarial weights to assess their impact on demographic shortcut reliance and overall performance. Results The multiview encoder raised the mean area under the curve (AUC) across clinical tasks from 0.742 to 0.831 compared with the foundation model embedding (ΔAUC +0.090; 95% CI: 0.078-0.100), with significant gains in 20 of 21 tasks. The embeddings remained robust with a limited number of views (mean ΔAUC +0.071; 95% CI: 0.043-0.113). Adversarial learning reduced sex and race predictability only at strong weights and at substantial cost to clinical performance. Conclusions The multiview encoder framework integrates multiple echocardiographic views into unified study-level embeddings, enabling substantial diagnostic improvements across diverse cardiac tasks. By producing compact, informative embeddings without requiring extensive computational resources, this approach lowers the cost of building echocardiographic AI on an existing foundation model.

title: Heart Failure Phenotyping and Prognosis by CMR-Derived Oxygen Delivery and Extraction.
abstract: Background Heart failure reflects impaired matching of systemic oxygen delivery to metabolic demand, yet resting oxygen transport is seldom measured. Objectives The purpose of this study was to noninvasively derive resting oxygen delivery and extraction using cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) and relate these to clinical characteristics and outcomes. Methods In this retrospective study, in patients with heart failure referred for clinical CMR, cardiac output was assessed by cine imaging; basal blood-pool T2 mapping provided imaging-derived venous oxygen saturation; and measured hemoglobin enabled calculation of arterial oxygen content. Arterial oxygen saturation was fixed at 96%. We derived indexed systemic oxygen delivery (DO 2 i), oxygen extraction fraction (OEF), and indexed systemic oxygen consumption (VO 2 i). The endpoint was all-cause death or heart failure hospitalization. Results A total of 429 patients were included (62 events). VO 2 i varied widely (tertile means 138.8, 207.9, and 293.8 mL/min/m 2 ), while left ventricular ejection fraction did not differ (38.8%, 40.6%, and 40.3%; P = 0.42). Imaging-derived venous oxygen saturation decreased across increasing VO 2 i tertiles (61.5%, 54.3%, and 50.7%; P < 0.0001). In Cox regression adjusted for age, sex, ejection fraction, and late gadolinium enhancement, VO 2 i was associated with the endpoint (HR: 1.15 per 50 mL/min/m 2 , 95% CI: 1.00-1.32; P = 0.046), but discrimination of VO 2 i alone was poor (Harrell's C = 0.53). Delivery-extraction phenotypes differed in event risk (log-rank P = 0.026): event proportions were 8.6% (high DO 2 i/low OEF), 14.0% (low DO 2 i/low OEF), 16.8% (high DO 2 i/high OEF), and 18.3% (low DO 2 i/high OEF). The delivery-extraction phenotype remained associated with outcome after adjustment for age, sex, left ventricular ejection fraction, and CMR-derived filling pressure. Conclusions In this hypothesis-generating study, CMR-based oxygen supply-demand assessment delineates resting delivery-extraction phenotypes associated with heart failure outcomes.

title: Management of Coronary Calcified Nodules: A Position Statement.
abstract: Coronary calcified nodules are an uncommon but important substrate for acute coronary syndromes, stent underexpansion, and recurrent target lesion revascularization. This consensus integrates pathologic, imaging, prognostic, and interventional evidence to guide practical decision-making. Intravascular imaging is essential for diagnosis, mechanism definition, and procedural optimization. Optical coherence tomography provides superior assessment of cap disruption and thrombus, whereas intravascular ultrasound remains valuable when contrast exposure or lesion crossing limits optical coherence tomography. Treatment should be tailored to lesion crossability, calcium distribution, and the need for mechanical scaffolding. No calcium-modification device or drug-eluting stent vs drug-coated balloon strategy has demonstrated consistent superiority. The proposed type IIa/IIb framework is hypothesis-generating and requires prospective validation. Calcified nodule-related target lesion failure should be managed by correcting the dominant mechanical mechanism before antiproliferative therapy. These recommendations emphasize individualized, imaging-guided percutaneous coronary intervention and identify priorities for prospective comparative research.

title: Transcatheter Solution to Atypical Anomalous Pulmonary Venous Drainage in a Single Ventricle Patient.
abstract: Background Partial anomalous pulmonary venous drainage (PAPVD) is typically incompatible with single ventricle physiology if left unrepaired before cavopulmonary connection. This report describes a rare anatomical variant and novel interventional solution. Case summary An 8-month-old female with hypoplastic left heart variant developed profound cyanosis following bidirectional Glenn because of unrepaired PAPVD of the right upper pulmonary vein to the superior vena cava (SVC). Retrospective 3-dimensional reconstruction of the patient's neonatal computed tomography angiogram revealed a small interlobar vessel between the anomalous pulmonary vein and the anatomically normal right lower pulmonary vein. This interlobar vessel's gross dilatation and anatomical features permitted percutaneous device occlusion of the PAPVD connection to the SVC, isolating SVC return to the cavopulmonary circulation while preserving unobstructed pulmonary venous return to the atrium. Discussion Surgical and interventional solutions are reviewed in the context of this unusual anatomical variant. Take-home messages In the uncommon circumstance of an unrecognized anomalous pulmonary vein with connections to both systemic and pulmonary venous circulations, consideration may be given to interventional occlusion of the PAPVD connection to the systemic vein. Retrospective application of contemporary 3-dimensional reconstruction tools can add great value in delineating complex or unusual anatomy.

title: Sarcomatoid Renal Cell Carcinoma With Cardiac Metastasis Causing Right Ventricular Outflow Tract Obstruction.
abstract: Background Renal cell carcinoma (RCC) rarely metastasizes to the heart, and an aggressive histologic transformation known as sarcomatoid dedifferentiation confers a poor prognosis. Case summary A patient presented with progressive exertional dyspnea. Initial laboratory studies revealed elevated troponin and elevated D-dimer. Computed tomography pulmonary angiography showed a right ventricle (RV) filling defect. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated a large lobulated mass extending from the RV free wall into the outflow tract, encroaching on the pulmonic valve with an ejection fraction of <20%. Abdominal magnetic resonance imaging revealed a right renal mass. The patient suffered a fatal arrest because of obstructive shock from severe RV outflow tract obstruction. Discussion Postmortem examination confirmed metastatic sarcomatoid RCC. Patients typically present with advanced disease, and survival is <1 year. Combination immunotherapy is approved for metastatic RCC. Initiating immunotherapy would not have addressed the patient's acute hemodynamic compromise. Take-home message Early recognition of metastatic RCC is crucial for potential therapeutic intervention, though prognosis remains poor in advanced cases.

title: True Left-Ventricular Aneurysm After Ventricular Tachycardia Ablation: The Role of Imaging in a Rare Complication.
abstract: Background Left ventricular (LV) pseudoaneurysm is an uncommon but recognized complication of ventricular tachycardia (VT) ablation. In contrast, true LV aneurysm has been reported only rarely. Case summary Transthoracic echocardiogram, supported by cardiovascular magnetic resonance imaging, initially suggested an LV pseudoaneurysm in a patient after VT ablation. During evaluation for percutaneous closure, left ventriculogram and 3-dimensional transesophageal echocardiogram revealed more complex anatomy, prompting referral for surgical repair. Intraoperative findings confirmed a true LV aneurysm. Discussion True LV aneurysm may represent a rare complication of deep radiofrequency energy delivery during catheter ablation resulting in myocardial injury. Because differentiating true aneurysms from pseudoaneurysms can be challenging, a multimodality imaging approach may improve anatomical characterization, guide management, and enhance understanding of the underlying mechanism. Take-home message Multimodality imaging can improve anatomical characterization and procedural planning in patients with the rare complication of true left aneurysm after catheter ablation.

title: Antegrade Dissection and Re-Entry for Recanalization of Traumatic Coronary Artery Dissection.
abstract: Background Traumatic coronary artery dissection (TCAD) is a rare catastrophic complication of blunt chest trauma, often masked by concomitant injuries, posing diagnostic and therapeutic challenges. Case summary A 20-year-old man with polytrauma after a motorcycle accident developed cardiogenic shock. Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) suggested occlusive left anterior descending dissection, confirmed by delayed angiography under extracorporeal membrane oxygenation support. Stingray-based antegrade dissection and re-entry (ADR) with cutting balloon fenestration and drug-coated balloon angioplasty achieved TIMI flow grade 3. Three-month follow-up showed favorable left anterior descending healing and improved cardiac function. Discussion CCTA enables early TCAD diagnosis. ADR facilitates guidewire passage, and a stentless strategy is preferable in young polytrauma patients at high bleeding risk. Take-home messages Maintain suspicion for TCAD after blunt chest trauma, especially with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction features. CCTA aids early diagnosis; ADR-based percutaneous coronary intervention with drug-coated balloon is safe and effective.

title: "Whiplash Motion" in Cardiac Intimal Sarcoma With Functional Mitral Stenosis and Dynamic LVOT Obstruction.
abstract: Background Cardiac intimal sarcoma (CIS) usually presents as an isolated left atrial mass; pan-left-heart involvement producing simultaneous inflow and outflow obstruction is rare. Case summary A 43-year-old man presented in acute heart failure (B-type natriuretic peptide 948.8 pg/mL; right ventricular systolic pressure 59 mm Hg). Imaging showed a tumor in the left atrium and ventricle: an atrial mass infiltrated the mitral leaflet, causing functional mitral stenosis, whereas a mobile papillary-muscle component showed a "whiplash motion," prolapsing into the left ventricular outflow tract and protruding through the aortic valve in systole. Emergency debulking and mechanical mitral valve replacement followed; histopathology confirmed CIS (mouse double minute 2 homolog/cyclin-dependent kinase 4 positive, mouse double minute 2 homolog-amplified). Although adjuvant carbon-ion radiotherapy provided temporary control, the patient died 20 months later. Discussion We propose the "whiplash motion" sign and highlight the trade-off between mechanical-valve durability and bleeding risk during thoracic radiotherapy. Take-home message CIS can cause dual left-heart obstruction through multicomponent tumor dynamics; prosthetic valve choice should anticipate multimodality oncologic management.

title: Concomitant Wire-Loop Repositioning and Transapical Valve Replacement for a Migrated Sutureless Aortic Valve.
abstract: Background Sutureless aortic prosthesis migration is rare but potentially catastrophic. Case summary A 78-year-old woman on hemodialysis underwent minimally invasive double valve replacement using a sutureless aortic bioprosthesis. Failure to wean from cardiopulmonary bypass prompted intraoperative angiography, which raised suspicion of cranial migration of the aortic prosthesis, with bilateral coronary hypoperfusion; subsequent computed tomography confirmed the diagnosis. Because repositioning after surgical excision of the native leaflets would cause severe aortic regurgitation, a transapical transcatheter valve was prepositioned before transfemoral wire-loop repositioning. Coronary flow was restored, the failed valve was replaced, and 5-month follow-up showed preserved ventricular function and stable frame position. Discussion Prepositioning a transapical transcatheter valve before wire-loop repositioning enabled immediate valve replacement while minimizing the empty-annulus interval. Take-home message Failed passage of a Perceval sizer should preclude sutureless implantation; prepositioned transapical valve replacement with wire-loop repositioning is a viable bailout.

title: Miniaturizing Slipstream and Tip Detection to a 7-F Transradial System for Chronic Total Occlusion PCI.
abstract: Objective To demonstrate that the combination of the slipstream and tip detection can be miniaturized to a 7-F radial system using the SIDEPASS short-monorail dual-lumen catheter and AnteOwl intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) for a chronic total occlusion (CTO) lesion. Key steps Treat the in-stent restenosis in left circumflex artery #14 and insert the AnteOwl IVUS over the same wire (first-wire lumen only) to delineate the spatial relationship between the stent struts and the jailed ostium of left circumflex artery #15 CTO. Advance the SIDEPASS short-monorail dual-lumen catheter over the same wire within a 7-F guiding catheter, pass a second guidewire through an optimal stent-strut cell into the CTO, and complete lesion preparation. Potential pitfalls Narrow clearance within a 7-F guide, first-wire instability when removing the dual-lumen catheter, and inaccurate ostium identification can hinder the procedure. Take-home messages Miniaturizing slipstream and tip detection to a 7-F system provides a smaller radial access footprint for complex CTO percutaneous coronary intervention while preserving advanced IVUS-guided wiring.

title: Long-Term Prognostic Value of Scar Characteristics in Cardiac Magnetic Resonance to Predict Appropriate Therapies in Primary Prevention.
abstract: Background Cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) with late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) provides unique insights into ventricular arrhythmogenic substrate, although few studies have analyzed its long-term value in patients with implantable cardioverter-defibrillators (ICDs) for primary prevention. Objectives The aim of this study was to evaluate the role of LGE characteristics in stratifying arrhythmogenic risk in patients with ICD implantation for primary prevention over long-term follow-up. Methods This was a prospective study, between 2011 and 2017, in which 226 patients who underwent LGE CMR before ICD implantation for primary prevention were consecutively enrolled. Dedicated software (ADAS 3D) was used to quantify LGE, border zone, core, and conducting channels (CCs). Results The median age was 62.9 years (Q1-Q3: 55.4-68.5 years), with 52% of participants (n = 104) with ischemic cardiomyopathy and a median MADIT (Multicenter Automatic Defibrillator Implantation Trial) score of 54 (Q1-Q3: 42-64). After a median follow-up period of 8.1 years (Q1-Q3: 6.2-10 years), 59 patients (29.5%) reached the primary endpoint (appropriate ICD therapy). LGE mass >10 g (HR: 3.58; 95% CI: 1.29-9.93; P = 0.014), CCs (HR: 3.42; 95% CI: 1.69-6.96; P = 0.009), and the presence of both LGE mass >10 g and CCs (34.92% vs 5.55%; HR: 4.65; 95% CI: 1.46-14.8; P = 0.009) were strongly associated with the primary endpoint. Patients without CCs and with LGE mass < 10 g had a very low rate of appropriate therapies (negative predictive value = 92%). LGE parameters remained independently associated with the primary endpoint after adjustment for MADIT score. Conclusions The characteristics of potential arrhythmia substrate assessed using LGE CMR are potent predictors of ventricular arrhythmias after ICD implantation for the primary prevention of sudden death.

LGE mass >10 g (HR: 3.58; 95% CI: 1.29-9.93; P = 0.014), CCs (HR: 3.42; 95% CI: 1.69-6.96; P = 0.009), and the presence of both LGE mass >10 g and CCs (34.92% vs 5.55%; HR: 4.65; 95% CI: 1.46-14.8; P = 0.009) were strongly associated with the primary endpoint. Patients without CCs and with LGE mass < 10 g had a very low rate of appropriate therapies (negative predictive value = 92%). LGE parameters remained independently associated with the primary endpoint after adjustment for MADIT score.

Conclusions

The characteristics of potential arrhythmia substrate assessed using LGE CMR are potent predictors of ventricular arrhythmias after ICD implantation for the primary prevention of sudden death.

title: Association of Left Ventricular Epicardial Adipose Tissue and Lipomatous Metaplasia With Ventricular Tachycardia Circuitry and Recurrence Following Ablation in Patients With Non-Ischemic Cardiomyopathy.
abstract: Background Patients with nonischemic cardiomyopathy (NICM) have complex intramural ventricular tachycardia (VT) circuitry and relatively high postablation recurrences. Objectives This study evaluated the association of left ventricular epicardial adipose tissue (LV EAT) and lipomatous metaplasia (LM) with critical VT circuitry and postablation VT recurrence in patients with NICM. Methods In this retrospective study, we quantified LV EAT and LM via cardiac contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CECT) in a cohort of consecutive patients with NICM before VT ablation. CECT image registration with VT critical sites in electroanatomic mapping was performed in a subset. Mixed-effects and subdistribution proportional hazard models were used to examine the association of image features with VT circuitry elements and outcomes, respectively. Results In 48 patients with coregistered CECT-electroanatomic mapping, segmental maximal EAT thickness was associated with critical VT sites (OR: 1.36 per mm increase; P < 0.001), and a threshold of >4.7 mm EAT achieved 72% sensitivity and 71% specificity (OR: 2.15; P = 0.006) for VT site identification. This association remained significant after adjusting for LM, with a significant EAT-LM interaction (P = 0.027). Among all 119 patients, 52 experienced VT recurrence during a median follow-up of 1.7 years (Q1-Q3: 0.7-4.0). Lower LV EAT attenuation was independently associated with time to VT recurrence (subdistribution HR: 1.04 per 1 HU decrease; P = 0.012) after multivariable adjustment including LM and a significant LM interaction (P = 0.020). Conclusions LV EAT density and thickness are associated with VT circuitry and postablation recurrence in patients with NICM, and demonstrate a significant statistical interaction with LM.

title: Natural History, Pathogenesis, and Early Detection of Asplenia in Autoimmune Polyendocrinopathy-Candidiasis-Ectodermal Dystrophy.
abstract: Background Autoimmune polyendocrinopathy-candidiasis-ectodermal dystrophy (APECED) is characterized by interferon-γ (IFN-γ)-mediated immune dysregulation. Although asplenia has been reported in APECED, its prevalence, pathogenesis, and optimal strategies for early detection remain incompletely characterized. Objective To define the natural history of asplenia in APECED, elucidate its immunopathogenesis, and identify clinical correlates that may enable earlier recognition. Methods We evaluated two large APECED cohorts (n=170) for prevalence, timing, and clinical features of asplenia. Longitudinal imaging, peripheral blood smears (PBS), and hematologic parameters were analyzed. Mechanistic studies were performed in AIRE-deficient mice. Functional splenic imaging with liver-spleen 99m Tc-sulfur colloid single-photon emission computed tomography (SC-SPECT/CT) was performed in selected patients. Results Asplenia was identified in 17-20% of patients across both cohorts with onset from childhood to adulthood, a cumulative risk approaching ∼40% by age 40, and enrichment among patients with severe multiorgan disease. Longitudinal imaging demonstrated progressive decline in splenic volume over years. PBS abnormalities appeared late, whereas SC-SPECT/CT imaging revealed markedly impaired splenic function earlier. In AIRE-deficient mice, splenic destruction developed in an age-dependent manner, was associated with increased IFN-γ activity, and was prevented by Ifng ablation. Persistent leukocytosis and/or thrombocytosis were present in 93.8% of patients with asplenia and frequently preceded diagnosis by months to years, whereas such abnormalities were uncommon and transient in patients without asplenia. Conclusions Asplenia is a common, acquired, IFN-γ-dependent manifestation of APECED characterized by a prolonged subclinical phase. PBS examination is insensitive for early detection. Persistent leukocytosis and/or thrombocytosis may serve as accessible clinical correlates for early recognition.

title: Development of an Electronic Clinical Quality Measure for Excessive Radiation Dose or Inadequate Image Quality in Diagnostic CT in Adults.
abstract: The Excessive Radiation Dose or Inadequate Image Quality for Diagnostic CT in Adults (ExRad) measure is the first automated radiology outcome measure adopted by CMS. We describe its development, specification, calculation, and adoption. Beginning in 2018, the measure was developed under a CMS cooperative agreement following the Measures Management System Blueprint, with oversight from a multidisciplinary Technical Expert Panel. ExRad evaluates each adult diagnostic CT examination in three steps. First, the examination is assigned to 1 of 19 CT categories defined by anatomic region and clinical indication using International Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision, Clinical Modification and Current Procedural Terminology codes. Second, size-adjusted radiation dose and image noise are computed from the DICOM dose report and pixel data; because clinical and radiology data reside in separate systems, translation software inside the hospital firewall performs the linkage and calculations automatically. Third, dose and noise are compared with category-specific thresholds derived from a reader study in which 125 radiologists rated the image quality of 734 CT examinations. An examination is out of range if either value exceeds its threshold, and the measure score is the percentage of eligible examinations that are out of range. Testing across 32 facilities in eight health systems confirmed the availability, accuracy, validity, and reproducibility of all data elements, and the National Quality Forum endorsed the measure in 2021. CMS adopted ExRad in 2023 into hospital inpatient, hospital outpatient, and clinician quality reporting programs, with voluntary reporting beginning in 2025. It is the sole outcome measure in the Diagnostic Radiology MIPS (Merit-Based Incentive Payment System) Value Pathway.

title: Standalone commercial artificial intelligence software for pulmonary nodule detection on chest radiographs: a systematic review.
abstract: Background Pulmonary nodules may be missed on chest radiographs despite their clinical relevance for early lung cancer detection. Commercial artificial intelligence (AI) systems are increasingly available for chest radiograph interpretation, but evidence for their standalone performance remains fragmented across products, datasets, operating thresholds, and comparator designs. Purpose To systematically evaluate the standalone diagnostic performance of commercially available AI software for pulmonary nodule detection on chest radiographs compared with radiologists reading alone, and to identify methodological factors shaping interpretation of the evidence. Methods A systematic review was conducted according to PRISMA 2020 guidelines and registered with PROSPERO (CRD420261383905). PubMed, PubMed Central, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched. Eligible studies evaluated commercially available AI systems as standalone detectors for pulmonary nodules on chest radiographs and directly compared their performance with radiologists reading alone using an accepted clinical reference standard. Risk of bias was assessed using an adapted QUADAS-2 framework. Findings were synthesized narratively because of heterogeneity in study design, populations, reference standards, operating thresholds, and outcome measures. Results Six studies met the inclusion criteria, comprising 12 product-level evaluations across 10 commercial AI systems. Standalone AI performance varied: some evaluations showed AI exceeding radiologist-level performance, others showed no significant difference, and one showed AI below individual reader performance with approximately twice the false-positive rate. In the only standardized within-study comparison of multiple commercial products on the same dataset, four of seven systems significantly exceeded mean radiologist AUC. Standalone AI AUC ranged from 0.79 to 0.93 against a mean reader AUC of 0.81 (95% CI 0.77-0.85), indicating that performance varied among cleared products even when tested under identical conditions. Interpretation was limited by differences in operating thresholds, comparator design, reference standards, study populations, and outcome reporting. Risk-of-bias concerns were common, particularly in patient selection. Conclusions In the available peer-reviewed evidence, standalone commercial AI systems for chest radiograph pulmonary nodule detection show variable performance. Evidence remains insufficient to support class-wide standalone deployment because all studies were retrospective or reader-study based, thresholds were inconsistently reported, and real-world false-positive burden remains uncertain. Prospective real world evaluation with clearly reported operating thresholds, standardized comparator designs and complete diagnostic performance are needed.

title: CT-Based Deep Learning Assessment of Aortic Valve Fibrosis and Calcification: Development and Multicenter External Validation Against Experts, Histology, and Outcomes.
abstract: Background Computed tomography angiography (CTA) enables assessment of aortic valve tissue composition, providing insights into disease progression and helping predict outcomes in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement for severe aortic stenosis (AS). The authors aimed to develop a deep learning system for CTA-based quantification of aortic fibrotic and calcific tissue, validate its agreement with expert manual analysis and histopathology, and evaluate its value for outcome prediction. Methods This international, multicenter study included 1,674 patients who underwent CTA at 9 sites. A deep learning model based on the nnU-Net architecture was trained in 468 patients and applied to an external test set of 1,206 patients, including 29 with valve histology and 12 with serial CTA. title: Clinical and functional outcomes following transoral endoscopically-assisted treatment of mandibular subcondylar fractures: A single-center experience.
abstract: Purpose Evidence on the outcomes of transoral endoscopically-assisted treatment of mandibular subcondylar fractures remains limited. The primary aim of this study was to evaluate surgical outcomes, complication rates, revision rates, and long-term functional results following transoral endoscopically-assisted treatment of subcondylar fractures. The secondary aim was to identify predictors of postoperative complications, revision surgery, and craniomandibular dysfunction. Methods This monocentric observational study comprised a retrospective and a prospective study arm. The retrospective cohort included all patients with mandibular subcondylar fractures treated by transoral endoscopically-assisted open reduction and internal fixation without transbuccal trocars between December 2014 and August 2024. Fractures were classified using the AO CMF and Spiessl-Schroll Classification Systems based on preoperative CT imaging. Demographic, clinical, radiographic, surgical, and postoperative data were collected. The prospective cohort consisted of patients who underwent standardized clinical follow-up at least 12 months after surgery, including assessment of temporomandibular disorders, mandibular function, occlusion, pain, and maximum mouth opening using standardized DGFDT examination protocols. Primary outcomes were postoperative complications and revision surgery; long-term functional outcome was evaluated as a tertiary endpoint. Descriptive statistics, exploratory bivariate analyses, and multivariable logistic regression were performed to identify factors associated with postoperative complications. Results A total of 132 patients with 144 subcondylar fractures were included. Postoperative complications occurred in 43.8 % of fractures, whereas intraoperative revision following 3D C-arm imaging and postoperative revision surgery were required in 15.3 % and 2.8 % of cases, respectively. The most common complications were malocclusion (20.1 %), osteosynthesis material failure (15.3 %), and wound infection (14.6 %). Multivariable analysis identified longer intermaxillary fixation as the only independent predictor of postoperative complications (OR 1.052, 95 % CI 1.008-1.109; p = 0.036). Follow-up examinations demonstrated generally favorable long-term functional outcomes, although 22.7 % of patients showed signs of temporomandibular disorders and 31.8 % presented with objective occlusal disturbances. Conclusions Transoral Endoscopically-assisted open reduction and internal fixation provided reliable surgical management of subcondylar mandibular fractures, with a low revision rate and favorable long-term functional outcomes. Prolonged postoperative intermaxillary fixation was the only independent predictor of postoperative complications, while routine intraoperative 3D imaging supported accurate fracture reduction and implant positioning.

title: Evaluation of the accuracy of zygomaticomaxillary complex fracture reduction and fixation using a fully digital workflow versus conventional protocol: a randomized clinical trial.
abstract: The zygomatic bone has multiple points of articulation with the craniofacial skeleton, and accurate intraoperative reduction in various planes is very challenging and entirely dependent on the operator's subjective evaluation. This study aimed to investigate the efficiency of a novel fully digital protocol versus the conventional management strategy for zygomaticomaxillary complex fracture reduction and fixation. Twenty-eight patients with acute zygomatic fractures who met the inclusion criteria were recruited; each group of 14 patients was randomly assigned. The intervention group received a fully digital protocol, represented by customized predictive-hole surgical guides and patient-specific fixation plates, while the control group was managed conventionally. Accuracy of bone reduction was the primary outcome. The results showed that, when comparing the virtual reduction of both groups with the postoperative CT scans, the overall accuracy was markedly higher in the digital group (0.290 ± 0.132 mm) than in the conventional group (1.290 ± 0.525 mm), with a mean difference of -1.000 mm (95% CI -1.309 to -0.691; p < 0.001) and a very large effect size (d = -2.612). Clinically, the digital group showed higher patient satisfaction with aesthetics and a shorter operation duration, while no difference in infraorbital nerve numbness was observed between the two groups. Based on the statistical and clinical findings of this study, a fully digital workflow provided a valuable approach for the management of zygomaticomaxillary complex fractures, optimizing aesthetic and functional rehabilitation.
